Scaling N40,000 up by 600/500 would give N48,000, but that wrongly increases the fixed cost as well. Options A and B roughly double the cost, and C, N44,000, is too low for 600 items.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A computer chip manufacturer estimates that q (thousand) chips will be purchased by wholesalers when the price is p = 90 - 0.1q^2 naira per chip, and the same quantity of chips will be supplied when the price is p = 50 + q + 0.2q^2 naira per chip. The equilibrium price is
questions.explanation: At equilibrium demand price equals supply price: 90 - 0.1q^2 = 50 + q + 0.2q^2, so 0.3q^2 + q - 40 = 0, giving q = [-1 + sqrt(1 + 48)]/0.6 = 10 (the negative root is rejected). Then p = 90 - 0.1(10)^2 = N80. Option C, 10, is the equilibrium quantity, not the price.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A computer chip manufacturer estimates that q (thousand) chips will be purchased by wholesalers when the price is p = 90 - 0.1q^2 naira per chip, and the same quantity of chips will be supplied when the price is p = 50 + q + 0.2q^2 naira per chip. The equilibrium quantity (in thousands of chips) is
questions.explanation: Setting 90 - 0.1q^2 = 50 + q + 0.2q^2 gives 0.3q^2 + q - 40 = 0, or 3q^2 + 10q - 400 = 0, which factorises as (3q + 40)(q - 10) = 0, so q = 10 thousand chips. Check: demand price 90 - 10 = 80 and supply price 50 + 10 + 20 = 80 agree, whereas q = 20 (option B) gives 50 and 150, which do not match.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Two competing products have demand and supply functions qd1 = 100 - 2p1 + 3p2, qs1 = 2p1 - 4, qd2 = 150 + 4p1 - p2 and qs2 = 3p2 - 6, where p1 and p2 are the prices per unit of products 1 and 2. Find the equilibrium prices.
questions.explanation: Setting qd1 = qs1 gives 100 - 2p1 + 3p2 = 2p1 - 4, i.e. 4p1 - 3p2 = 104, and setting qd2 = qs2 gives 150 + 4p1 - p2 = 3p2 - 6, i.e. -4p1 + 4p2 = 156. Adding the two equations gives p2 = 260, and then 4p1 = 104 + 780 = 884, so p1 = 221. Option B comes from writing 100 - 4 instead of 100 + 4 in the first equation, option D from writing 150 - 6 instead of 150 + 6 in the second, and option A swaps the two prices.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Two competing products have demand and supply functions qd1 = 100 - 2p1 + 3p2, qs1 = 2p1 - 4, qd2 = 150 + 4p1 - p2 and qs2 = 3p2 - 6, where p1 and p2 are the prices per unit of products 1 and 2. Find the equilibrium quantities q1 and q2.
questions.explanation: Equating demand and supply for each product gives 4p1 - 3p2 = 104 and -4p1 + 4p2 = 156, which solve to p1 = 221 and p2 = 260. Then q1 = 2(221) - 4 = 438 and q2 = 3(260) - 6 = 774 (check: qd2 = 150 + 884 - 260 = 774). Option A leaves out the constants -4 and -6 in the supply functions, option B adds them instead of subtracting, and option C swaps the two quantities.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply equations of a product are (q + 20)(p + 10) = 400 and q = 2p - 7 respectively, where p is price and q is quantity. Find the equilibrium price and quantity.
questions.explanation: Substituting q = 2p - 7 into the demand equation gives (2p + 13)(p + 10) = 400, so 2p^2 + 33p + 130 = 400, i.e. 2p^2 + 33p - 270 = 0, which factorises as (2p + 45)(p - 6) = 0. Since a price cannot be negative, p = 6 and q = 2(6) - 7 = 5 (check: 25 x 16 = 400). Option D is the other root of the quadratic, which must be rejected because price and quantity cannot be negative, and option B swaps the price and the quantity.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer of cassette tapes has a fixed cost of N60,000 and a variable cost of N4 per cassette produced. Each cassette sells for N7. At what sales (revenue) volume will break-even occur?
questions.explanation: The break-even quantity is q = F/(p - v) = 60,000/(7 - 4) = 20,000 cassettes, so break-even revenue is R = 7 x 20,000 = N140,000, which equals C = 4(20,000) + 60,000. Option D multiplies 20,000 by the variable cost of N4 instead of the selling price, option A is just the fixed cost, and option B is the number of cassettes, not the naira value of sales.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer of cassette tapes has a fixed cost of N60,000 and a variable cost of N4 per cassette produced. Each cassette sells for N7. How much profit will be earned if 25,000 cassettes are produced and sold?
questions.explanation: Revenue is R = 7(25,000) = N175,000 and total cost is C = 4(25,000) + 60,000 = N160,000, so profit = 175,000 - 160,000 = N15,000. Option C forgets the fixed cost (3 x 25,000), option D forgets the variable cost (175,000 - 60,000), and option B subtracts revenue from cost; since 25,000 is above the break-even level of 20,000 cassettes, the firm must make a profit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A retailer's gross margin is to be 33% of the retail price, and other variable costs are estimated at N0.13 per naira of sales. Fixed cost is estimated at N4,000. What is the break-even sales volume, correct to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: Each naira of sales leaves a net margin of M = 0.33 - 0.13 = 0.20 towards fixed cost, so total cost is y = 0.80x + 4,000 and break-even sales are x = F/M = 4,000/0.20 = N20,000. Option B divides by the gross margin 0.33 and ignores the other variable costs, option D divides by 0.13, and option C divides by 0.80, which is the cost share of each naira rather than the margin.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A retailer's gross margin is to be 33% of the retail price, and other variable costs are estimated at N0.13 per naira of sales. Fixed cost is estimated at N4,000. Estimate the profit when sales are N50,000.
questions.explanation: The net margin is M = 0.33 - 0.13 = 0.20, so total cost is y = 0.80(50,000) + 4,000 = N44,000 and profit = 50,000 - 44,000 = N6,000. Option A uses the 33% margin without deducting the other variable costs (16,500 - 4,000), option B wrongly uses 0.13 as the margin (6,500 - 4,000), and option C forgets to subtract the fixed cost (0.20 x 50,000).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: What is meant by the break-even quantity of a firm?

options.a: The level of output at which profit is at its maximum
options.b: The level of output at which fixed cost equals total variable cost
options.c: The level of output at which total revenue equals total cost, so profit is zero
options.d: The level of output at which total revenue equals total variable cost

questions.explanation: At the break-even quantity total revenue just covers total cost (fixed plus variable), so the firm makes neither profit nor loss; with C = vq + F and R = pq it is q = F/(p - v). Below this output the firm makes a loss and above it a profit. Option A confuses break-even with profit maximisation, and option D ignores the fixed cost, which revenue must also cover.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Given the demand and supply functions for two competing products, qd1 = 82 - 3p1 + p2, qs1 = 15p1 - 5, qd2 = 92 + 2p1 - 4p2 and qs2 = 32p2 - 6, find the equilibrium quantities q1 and q2.
questions.explanation: Setting qd1 = qs1 gives 18p1 - p2 = 87, and setting qd2 = qs2 gives 2p1 - 36p2 = -98; substituting p2 = 18p1 - 87 into the second gives -646p1 = -3,230, so p1 = 5 and p2 = 3. Then q1 = 15(5) - 5 = 70 and q2 = 32(3) - 6 = 90, which match demand: 82 - 15 + 3 = 70 and 92 + 10 - 12 = 90. Option C leaves out the -5 and -6 in the supply functions, option A adds them instead, and option B swaps the two quantities.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply functions of a product are D = 17 - 4p - p^2 and S = 4p - 3, where p is the price per unit. Determine the equilibrium price and quantity.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium D = S, so 17 - 4p - p^2 = 4p - 3, giving p^2 + 8p - 20 = 0 = (p + 10)(p - 2). A price cannot be negative, so p = 2 and the quantity is S = 4(2) - 3 = 5 (and D = 17 - 8 - 4 = 5). Option D keeps the negative root, which makes no economic sense, option B comes from a sign slip giving p^2 - 8p - 20 = 0, and option A forgets the -p^2 term when finding D.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply equations of a product are 2p^2 + q^2 = 11 and p + 2q = 7 respectively, where p is price and q is quantity. Find the equilibrium price and quantity.
questions.explanation: From the supply equation p = 7 - 2q; substituting gives 2(7 - 2q)^2 + q^2 = 11, so 98 - 56q + 9q^2 = 11, i.e. 9q^2 - 56q + 87 = 0. The discriminant is 3,136 - 3,132 = 4, so q = (56 +/- 2)/18 = 3 or 29/9, giving p = 1 or 5/9; both pairs are positive and satisfy both equations. Option D swaps price and quantity, option B wrongly concludes the discriminant is negative, and option C fails the demand equation (2 + 16 = 18, not 11).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer of keyboards has a fixed cost of N10,000 and a variable cost of N5 per keyboard made. The selling price is N10 per keyboard. At what number of keyboards will break-even occur?
questions.explanation: Break-even happens where revenue equals cost: 10q = 5q + 10,000, so 5q = 10,000 and q = 2,000 keyboards, because each keyboard contributes N10 - N5 = N5 towards the N10,000 fixed cost. Option D divides the fixed cost by the selling price and forgets the variable cost, and Option B wrongly adds the variable cost to the price (10,000/15). Option C is the break-even revenue in naira (N20,000), not the number of units.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer of keyboards has a fixed cost of N10,000 and a variable cost of N5 per keyboard made. The selling price is N10 per keyboard. What is the profit or loss if 1,000 keyboards are produced and sold?
questions.explanation: At 1,000 units, revenue is R = 10(1,000) = N10,000 and total cost is C = 5(1,000) + 10,000 = N15,000, so profit = 10,000 - 15,000 = -N5,000, a loss of N5,000. Option B forgets the N10,000 fixed cost and treats the N5,000 contribution as profit. Option D is just the fixed cost and Option C is the total cost, not the loss.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer has a fixed cost of N7,500 and a variable cost of N7 per unit made. The selling price is N10 per unit. At what sales volume (revenue) will break-even occur?
questions.explanation: First find the break-even quantity: 10q = 7q + 7,500 gives 3q = 7,500, so q = 2,500 units. Break-even sales revenue is then 10 x 2,500 = N25,000 (check: cost = 7(2,500) + 7,500 = N25,000). Option C is only the fixed cost, Option B is only the variable cost at break-even, and Option A is the break-even quantity in units rather than the revenue in naira.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer of handbags has a fixed cost of N120,000 and a variable cost of N20 per unit made and sold. The selling price is N50 per unit. What is the profit if 10,000 handbags are made and sold?
questions.explanation: Profit is revenue minus total cost. At 10,000 handbags, R = 50(10,000) = N500,000 and C = 20(10,000) + 120,000 = N320,000, so profit = 500,000 - 320,000 = N180,000. Option D leaves out the fixed cost, Option B leaves out the variable cost, and Option C is the total cost rather than the profit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm's sales are N40,000, its fixed expense is N12,000 and its margin (the share of each naira of sales left after variable cost) is 25%. What are the total cost and the profit or loss?

options.a: Total cost N42,000; profit of N2,000
options.b: Total cost N30,000; profit of N10,000
options.c: Total cost N42,000; loss of N2,000
options.d: Total cost N22,000; profit of N18,000

questions.explanation: With a 25% margin, variable cost is 1 - 0.25 = 75% of sales, so total cost = 0.75(40,000) + 12,000 = 30,000 + 12,000 = N42,000. Since sales of N40,000 fall short of this, the firm makes a loss of 42,000 - 40,000 = N2,000. Option D wrongly treats the 25% as the variable cost, Option B leaves out the fixed expense, and Option A gets the cost right but calls the shortfall a profit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer's total cost consists of a fixed overhead of N200 plus production costs of N50 per unit. Express the total cost C as a function of the number of units x produced.
questions.explanation: Total cost = (cost per unit)(number of units) + fixed overhead, so C(x) = 50x + 200, a straight line with slope 50 (the cost of each extra unit) and intercept 200 (the fixed cost). Option A swaps the per-unit cost and the overhead, and option D wrongly charges the overhead on every unit. Option B subtracts the overhead even though it is an extra cost.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer can produce radios at a cost of N2 each. The radios have been selling for N5 each, and at this price consumers have been buying 4,000 radios a month. The manufacturer plans to raise the price and estimates that for each N1 increase in price, 400 fewer radios will be sold each month. Express the monthly profit P as a function of the selling price x.
questions.explanation: Profit = (number sold)(profit per radio). The price rise is x - 5, so the number sold is 4,000 - 400(x - 5) = 6,000 - 400x = 400(15 - x), and the profit per radio is x - 2, giving P(x) = 400(15 - x)(x - 2). Option C uses 4,000 - 400x, treating x as the price increase rather than the price, and option B subtracts the old selling price N5 instead of the N2 cost. Option A is revenue, because it leaves out the cost of each radio.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company determines that the cost of manufacturing belts is N2 each plus N300 per day in fixed costs. The company sells the belts for N3 each. What is the break-even point?
questions.explanation: Break-even is where revenue equals cost: R(x) = 3x and C(x) = 2x + 300, so 3x = 2x + 300 and x = 300 belts a day, because each belt contributes N3 - N2 = N1 towards the N300 fixed cost. Option B divides the fixed cost by the selling price and option C divides it by the unit cost, instead of by the N1 contribution per belt. Option A divides by the sum 3 + 2 = 5 rather than the difference.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company's cost of producing x items is C(x) = 500 + 140x, and the price it charges per item is p = 200 - x. Find the break-even point(s).
questions.explanation: Revenue is R(x) = px = 200x - x^2, and break-even means R(x) = C(x): 200x - x^2 = 500 + 140x, so x^2 - 60x + 500 = (x - 10)(x - 50) = 0, giving x = 10 and x = 50, with a profit for outputs between them. Option A comes from a sign slip in the factors, and option B is the profit-maximising output (where P'(x) = 0), not a break-even point. Option C multiplies to 500 but does not add up to 60.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company's cost of producing x items is C(x) = 500 + 140x, and the price it charges per item is p = 200 - x. Find the profit function P(x).
questions.explanation: Profit is revenue minus cost, where revenue R(x) = (200 - x)x = 200x - x^2. So P(x) = (200x - x^2) - (500 + 140x) = -x^2 + 60x - 500. Option B does not carry the minus sign through the bracket to the fixed cost 500, option D adds cost to revenue, and option C loses the minus sign on x^2 from the revenue.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The supply function for a commodity is S(p) = p^2 + 3p - 70 and the demand function is D(p) = 410 - p. Find the equilibrium price and the number of units supplied and demanded at that price.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium supply equals demand: p^2 + 3p - 70 = 410 - p, so p^2 + 4p - 480 = (p - 20)(p + 24) = 0. A price cannot be negative, so p = N20 and D(20) = 410 - 20 = 390 units (check: S(20) = 400 + 60 - 70 = 390). Option A turns the root -24 into +24, option D uses the demand intercept 410 instead of substituting p = 20, and option C comes from factorising the quadratic wrongly (S(12) = 110, not 398).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The total cost of manufacturing q units of a commodity is C(q) = q^3 - 30q^2 + 400q + 500 naira. Compute the total cost of manufacturing 20 units.
questions.explanation: Substitute q = 20: C(20) = 8,000 - 30(400) + 400(20) + 500 = 8,000 - 12,000 + 8,000 + 500 = N4,500. Option C leaves out the fixed cost of 500, and option A adds the 12,000 instead of subtracting it. Option D is C(19), the cost of only 19 units.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: At a certain factory, the total cost of manufacturing q units during the daily production run is C(q) = q^2 + q + 900 naira. On a typical workday, q(t) = 25t units are manufactured during the first t hours of a production run. How much will have been spent on production by the end of the 3rd hour?
questions.explanation: Compose the functions: C[q(t)] = (25t)^2 + 25t + 900 = 625t^2 + 25t + 900. At t = 3, C = 625(9) + 75 + 900 = 5,625 + 75 + 900 = N6,600, since 75 units have been made. Option A leaves out the N900 fixed cost, option B squares only t and not the 25 (using 25t^2), and option C puts t = 3 straight into C(q) as if only 3 units were made.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: At a certain factory, the total cost of manufacturing q units during the daily production run is C(q) = q^2 + q + 900 naira, and q(t) = 25t units are manufactured during the first t hours of a production run. When will the total manufacturing cost reach N11,000?
questions.explanation: As a function of time, C(t) = 625t^2 + 25t + 900, so 625t^2 + 25t + 900 = 11,000 gives 625t^2 + 25t - 10,100 = 0, whose positive root is t = 4 (check: 625(16) + 100 + 900 = 11,000). Option A solves q^2 + q + 900 = 11,000 to get q = 100 units but forgets to convert units into hours (100/25 = 4). Option B drops the N900 fixed cost, and option D confuses t^2 = 16 with t.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Revenue R equals the unit selling price p times the number x of units sold, R = xp. Suppose p and x are related by the demand equation p = -(1/10)x + 20, 0 <= x <= 200. Express the revenue R as a function of x.
questions.explanation: Multiply the demand price by the quantity: R(x) = x(-(1/10)x + 20) = -(1/10)x^2 + 20x, a downward-opening parabola. Option D is just the demand (price) equation, not revenue, and option B multiplies only the first term by x. Option C loses the minus sign, which would wrongly make revenue keep rising however many units are sold.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The price p (in naira) and the quantity x sold of a product obey the demand equation x = -5p + 100, 0 <= p <= 20. Express the revenue R = xp as a function of x and find the revenue when 15 units are sold.
questions.explanation: Solving the demand equation for price gives p = 20 - x/5, so R(x) = x(20 - x/5) = 20x - (1/5)x^2. When x = 15, R = 300 - 45 = N255 (each unit sells at N17). Option C treats 15 as the price instead of the quantity (that price sells 25 units), option B forgets the -(1/5)x^2 term, and option D inverts the demand equation wrongly as p = 100 - x/5.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer's total cost consists of a fixed overhead of N5,000 plus production costs of N60 per unit. Express the total cost as a function of the number of units x produced, and find the total cost of producing 100 units.
questions.explanation: The cost function is C(x) = 60x + 5,000, so C(100) = 60(100) + 5,000 = 6,000 + 5,000 = N11,000. Option D is only the variable cost and forgets the overhead, and option A adds the cost of just one unit to the overhead. Option B wrongly charges the N5,000 overhead on every unit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer has been selling radios at N5 each, and at this price consumers have been buying 4,000 radios a month. The manufacturer estimates that for each N1 increase in price, 400 fewer radios will be sold each month. Express the number of radios sold, y, as a linear function of the selling price x.
questions.explanation: The line passes through (5, 4,000) with slope -400, so y - 4,000 = -400(x - 5), giving y = 6,000 - 400x = 400(15 - x); at x = 5 this gives 400 x 10 = 4,000 as required. Option C is 4,000 - 400x, which measures x as the price increase rather than the price (at x = 5 it gives only 2,000), and option B has the wrong sign on the slope. Option A is -400(x - 5) with the starting sales of 4,000 left out, so it would mean zero sales at the current price.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Each unit of a certain commodity costs p = 35x + 15 kobo when x units of the commodity are produced. If all x units are sold at this price, express the revenue derived from the sales as a function of x.
questions.explanation: Revenue is price times quantity, so R(x) = x(35x + 15) = 35x^2 + 15x kobo. Option A is just the price of one unit, and option C multiplies only the 35x term by x. Option D is the derivative of the correct revenue, which is marginal revenue, not revenue.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A pharmacy sells two brands of aspirin: Brand A at N1.25 per bottle and Brand B at N1.50 per bottle. If x bottles of Brand A and y bottles of Brand B are sold, what is the revenue function, and what is the revenue when 100 bottles of Brand A and 150 bottles of Brand B are sold?
questions.explanation: Revenue from each brand is price times quantity, and total revenue is their sum: R(x, y) = 1.25x + 1.50y. Then R(100, 150) = 1.25(100) + 1.50(150) = 125 + 225 = N350. Option B matches the prices to the wrong quantities (1.25 x 150 + 1.50 x 100), option A adds the two prices and charges the total on every bottle, and option C multiplies the two brands' revenues instead of adding them.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Market research indicates that consumers will buy x thousand units of a particular kind of coffee maker when the unit price is p(x) = -0.27x + 51 naira. The cost of producing the x thousand units is C(x) = 2.23x^2 + 3.5x + 85 thousand naira. Which is the profit function P(x), in thousands of naira?
questions.explanation: Revenue is R(x) = x*p(x) = -0.27x^2 + 51x, and profit is P(x) = R(x) - C(x) = -0.27x^2 + 51x - 2.23x^2 - 3.5x - 85 = -2.5x^2 + 47.5x - 85. Option A subtracts only the x^2 term of C(x) and adds the other cost terms, option D combines -0.27x^2 and -2.23x^2 with the wrong sign, and option C adds the fixed cost 85 instead of subtracting it.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Market research indicates that consumers will buy x thousand units of a particular kind of coffee maker when the unit price is p(x) = -0.27x + 51 naira. The cost of producing the x thousand units is C(x) = 2.23x^2 + 3.5x + 85 thousand naira. For what values of x is production of the coffee makers profitable?
questions.explanation: Profit is P(x) = (-0.27x^2 + 51x) - (2.23x^2 + 3.5x + 85) = -2.5x^2 + 47.5x - 85 = -2.5(x - 2)(x - 17). Since the leading coefficient is negative, P(x) > 0 only between the roots, so production is profitable for 2 < x < 17 (between 2,000 and 17,000 units). Option B gives the regions where P(x) is negative (losses), option C ignores the fixed cost of 85, and option A forgets that profit turns negative again beyond x = 17.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Suppose the total cost in naira of manufacturing q units of a certain commodity is C(q) = q^3 - 30q^2 + 500q + 200. What is the cost of manufacturing 10 units of the commodity?
questions.explanation: Substitute q = 10: C(10) = 10^3 - 30(10)^2 + 500(10) + 200 = 1,000 - 3,000 + 5,000 + 200 = N3,200. Option B leaves out the fixed cost of 200, option C is C(9), the cost of 9 units, and option A treats -30q^2 as +3,000.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Suppose the total cost in naira of manufacturing q units of a certain commodity is C(q) = q^3 - 30q^2 + 500q + 200. What is the cost of manufacturing the 10th unit of the commodity?
questions.explanation: The cost of the 10th unit is the extra cost of going from 9 to 10 units: C(10) - C(9) = 3,200 - 2,999 = N201, where C(10) = 1,000 - 3,000 + 5,000 + 200 = 3,200 and C(9) = 729 - 2,430 + 4,500 + 200 = 2,999. Option C is the total cost of all 10 units, option D is the total cost of 9 units, and option A is the average cost 3,200/10, not the cost of the 10th unit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer can produce printer paper at a cost of N2 per ream. The paper has been selling for N5 per ream, and at that price consumers have been buying 4,000 reams a month. The manufacturer plans to raise the price and estimates that for each N1 increase in price, 400 fewer reams will be sold each month. Which expresses the monthly profit P as a function of the price p per ream?
questions.explanation: Profit is (number of reams sold)(profit per ream). Reams sold are 4,000 - 400(p - 5) = 6,000 - 400p and the profit per ream is p - 2, so P(p) = (6,000 - 400p)(p - 2) = -400p^2 + 6,800p - 12,000. Option B cuts 400 reams for every naira of the whole price instead of every naira above N5, option A is the revenue (6,000 - 400p)p and ignores the N2 cost, and option C subtracts the old price N5 instead of the cost N2.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer can produce printer paper at a cost of N2 per ream. The paper has been selling for N5 per ream, and at that price consumers have been buying 4,000 reams a month. The manufacturer plans to raise the price and estimates that for each N1 increase in price, 400 fewer reams will be sold each month. What price per ream maximizes monthly profit, and what is the maximum profit?

options.a: N6.00 per ream, giving a maximum profit of N6,400
options.b: N8.50 per ream, giving a maximum profit of N16,900
options.c: N7.50 per ream, giving a maximum profit of N22,500
options.d: N8.50 per ream, giving a maximum profit of N22,100

questions.explanation: Profit is P(p) = (6,000 - 400p)(p - 2) = -400p^2 + 6,800p - 12,000, a downward-opening parabola with vertex at p = -6,800/(2(-400)) = 8.5. The maximum profit is P(8.5) = (6,000 - 3,400)(6.5) = 2,600 x 6.5 = N16,900. Option C maximizes revenue and ignores the N2 cost, option A uses 4,000 - 400p for the number sold, and option D reports the revenue 2,600 x 8.5 at the right price instead of the profit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Manufacturers will supply x units of a commodity when the price is p = S(x) naira per unit, and consumers will demand x units when the price is p = D(x) naira per unit, where S(x) = x^2 + 14 and D(x) = 174 - 6x. At what level of production x and unit price p is market equilibrium achieved?
questions.explanation: At equilibrium supply equals demand: x^2 + 14 = 174 - 6x, so x^2 + 6x - 160 = 0 and (x - 10)(x + 16) = 0. A negative quantity makes no sense, so x = 10 and p = D(10) = 174 - 60 = N114 (check: S(10) = 100 + 14 = 114). Option D comes from a sign slip that gives x^2 - 6x - 160 = 0, option C keeps the rejected negative root, and option B is where the demand curve meets p = 0, not the equilibrium.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer can sell a certain product for N110 per unit. Total cost consists of a fixed overhead of N7,500 plus production costs of N60 per unit. How many units must the manufacturer sell to break even?
questions.explanation: Break-even is where revenue equals cost: 110x = 7,500 + 60x, so 50x = 7,500 and x = 150 units. Each unit contributes N110 - N60 = N50 towards the fixed overhead. Option B divides the overhead by the N60 unit cost instead of the N50 contribution, option D divides it by the N110 price, and option A is the contribution per unit, not a number of units.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturer can sell a certain product for N110 per unit. Total cost consists of a fixed overhead of N7,500 plus production costs of N60 per unit. How many units must be sold for the manufacturer to realize a profit of N1,250?
questions.explanation: Profit is P(x) = 110x - (7,500 + 60x) = 50x - 7,500. Setting 50x - 7,500 = 1,250 gives 50x = 8,750, so x = 175 units. Option C subtracts the target profit from the overhead instead of adding it, option A ignores the fixed overhead (1,250/50), and option D is the break-even level, where profit is zero.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The supply and demand functions for a product are given by S = 3p - 30 and D = 600/p, where p is the price charged for the product in naira. Find the price p for which the market is in equilibrium, and the corresponding demand.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium 3p - 30 = 600/p, so 3p^2 - 30p - 600 = 0, i.e. p^2 - 10p - 200 = (p - 20)(p + 10) = 0. Price cannot be negative, so p = N20 and demand D = 600/20 = 30 units (supply 3(20) - 30 = 30 agrees). Option A comes from a sign error in factorising (at p = 10 supply would be zero), Option B swaps the price and quantity, and Option C has the right price but works out the quantity as 3(20) = 60, forgetting the -30 in the supply function.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand for a made-in-Nigeria car is given by P = -14q + 740 and the supply for the same product is P = 10q - 220, where P is in thousand naira and q is quantity in thousands. Find the equilibrium price and quantity.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium -14q + 740 = 10q - 220, so 24q = 960 and q = 40, i.e. 40,000 cars; then P = 10(40) - 220 = 180, i.e. N180,000. Option A swaps price and quantity, Option C makes a sign slip in the demand equation (14(40) + 740 = 1,300), and Option D is a point on the demand curve only, since at P = 250 supply is 47,000 cars, not 35,000.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand for a made-in-Nigeria car is given by P = -14q + 740 and the supply for the same product is P = 10q - 220, where P is in thousand naira and q is quantity in thousands. Find the excess supply when the price is N350,000, giving your answer to the nearest thousand units.
questions.explanation: At P = 350 (thousand naira), supply gives 350 = 10q - 220, so q = 57 (57,000 cars), and demand gives 350 = -14q + 740, so q = 390/14 = 27.86 (about 28,000 cars). Excess supply = Qs - Qd = 57,000 - 27,857 = 29,143, which is 29,000 to the nearest thousand. Option A subtracts the wrong way round (Qd - Qs), Option C adds the two quantities, and Option D uses the quantity demanded at N250,000 (35,000) instead of at N350,000.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Find the equilibrium price and quantity given the functions Qd = 2 - 0.02p and Qs = 0.2 + 0.07p.
questions.explanation: Set Qd = Qs: 2 - 0.02p = 0.2 + 0.07p, so 1.8 = 0.09p and p = 20; then Q = 2 - 0.02(20) = 1.6, and Qs = 0.2 + 0.07(20) = 1.6 agrees. Option A subtracts the coefficients (0.07 - 0.02 = 0.05) instead of adding them, Option B adds 0.2 to 2 instead of subtracting it, and Option D has the right price but adds 0.4 instead of subtracting it.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Given the total cost function TC(Q) = 3600 - 177Q - 15Q^2 + 0.5Q^3, find the marginal cost (MC) function.
questions.explanation: MC = dTC/dQ: the fixed 3,600 differentiates to 0, -177Q gives -177, -15Q^2 gives -30Q and 0.5Q^3 gives 1.5Q^2, so MC = -177 - 30Q + 1.5Q^2. Option A keeps the fixed cost, which does not change with output, Option B is the average variable cost VC/Q, and Option C integrates TC instead of differentiating it.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Given the total cost function TC(Q) = 3600 - 177Q - 15Q^2 + 0.5Q^3, find the average variable cost (AVC) function.
questions.explanation: Fixed cost is TC(0) = 3,600, so VC = TC - FC = -177Q - 15Q^2 + 0.5Q^3, and AVC = VC/Q = -177 - 15Q + 0.5Q^2. Option B is average total cost, because it still includes AFC = 3600/Q, Option C is the marginal cost, and Option D is the variable cost itself, not divided by Q.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Given the demand and supply functions Qd = 60 - 0.8P and Qs = 10 + 0.2P, calculate the equilibrium price and quantity.
questions.explanation: Set Qd = Qs: 60 - 0.8P = 10 + 0.2P, so 50 = 1.0P and P = 50, with Q = 10 + 0.2(50) = 20 (and Qd = 60 - 40 = 20 agrees). Option B adds 60 and 10 instead of subtracting, Option C divides 50 by 0.8 alone, and Option D subtracts the coefficients (0.8 - 0.2 = 0.6) instead of adding them.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Given the demand and supply functions Qd = 60 - 0.8P and Qs = 10 + 0.2P, determine the excess demand when the price is decreased to 40 and the excess supply when the price is increased to 70.
questions.explanation: At P = 40, Qd = 60 - 32 = 28 and Qs = 10 + 8 = 18, so excess demand = Qd - Qs = 10. At P = 70, Qd = 60 - 56 = 4 and Qs = 10 + 14 = 24, so excess supply = Qs - Qd = 20. Option A takes both differences the wrong way round, Option B adds the quantities instead of subtracting, and Option C gives only the quantities supplied.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Given that the demand function of a firm is Q = 40 - P, find the marginal revenue (MR) function and state the type of market the firm is operating in.

options.a: MR = 40 - Q; a perfectly competitive market, since AR = MR
options.d: MR = 40 - 2Q; a monopolistic market, since AR > MR

questions.explanation: With inverse demand P = 40 - Q, TR = (40 - Q)Q = 40Q - Q^2, AR = TR/Q = 40 - Q and MR = dTR/dQ = 40 - 2Q. AR is greater than MR at every positive Q, which marks a monopolistic market (perfect competition needs AR = MR). Option A confuses MR with AR, Option B has the right MR but the wrong market type, and Option C gives TR instead of MR.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: For a new product, a manufacturer spends N100,000 on infrastructure and the variable cost is estimated at N150 per unit. The selling price is fixed at N200 per unit. What is the break-even point (to the nearest unit)?
questions.explanation: With C(x) = 100,000 + 150x and R(x) = 200x, profit is P(x) = 200x - (100,000 + 150x) = 50x - 100,000. At break-even P(x) = 0, so 50x = 100,000 and x = 2,000 units. Option A divides the fixed cost by the price alone and option C by the variable cost alone, but the fixed cost must be divided by the contribution per unit, 200 - 150 = N50; option D wrongly adds the price and variable cost.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company produces a product with fixed costs of N18,000. The variable cost is estimated to be 30% of the total revenue, and the product sells at N20 per unit. Which of the following is the profit function P(x)?
questions.explanation: Revenue is R(x) = 20x and the variable cost is 30% of revenue, 0.3 x 20x = 6x, so C(x) = 18,000 + 6x. Then P(x) = R(x) - C(x) = 20x - (18,000 + 6x) = 14x - 18,000. Option B treats the 6x variable cost as if it were the profit per unit, option D forgets the variable cost, and option A adds the fixed cost instead of subtracting it.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturing company finds that the daily cost of producing x items is C(x) = 210x + 7000. If each item is sold for N350, what is the minimum number of items that must be produced and sold daily to ensure no loss?
questions.explanation: Revenue is R(x) = 350x, so P(x) = 350x - (210x + 7000) = 140x - 7000. No loss needs P(x) >= 0, so 140x >= 7000 and x >= 50, meaning at least 50 items a day. Option C divides 7000 by the selling price only, option B divides it by the variable cost, and option D is the contribution per item (350 - 210 = 140), not a number of items.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A manufacturing company finds that the daily cost of producing x items is C(x) = 210x + 7000. Each item was selling for N350. If the selling price is increased by N35 per item, what is the new break-even point (to the nearest whole item)?
questions.explanation: The new price is 350 + 35 = N385, so P(x) = 385x - (210x + 7000) = 175x - 7000. Setting P(x) = 0 gives x = 7000/175 = 40 items. Option D subtracts the N35 instead of adding it (7000/105, about 67), option A divides the fixed cost by the N35 increase alone, and option B divides by the new price instead of the new contribution per item.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The fixed cost of a new product is N18,000 and the variable cost per unit is N550. If the demand function is p(x) = 4000 - 150x, find the break-even values of x (to the nearest whole unit where necessary).
questions.explanation: Revenue is R = px = 4000x - 150x^2 and cost is C = 18,000 + 550x, so break-even needs 4000x - 150x^2 = 18,000 + 550x, that is 150x^2 - 3450x + 18,000 = 0. Dividing by 150 gives x^2 - 23x + 120 = 0, so (x - 8)(x - 15) = 0 and x = 8 or x = 15. Option B leaves out the variable cost, option C adds the variable cost to revenue instead of subtracting it, and option D is a sign slip when factorising.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company spends N25,000 on infrastructure and the variable cost of producing one item is N45. If the item is sold for N65, find the break-even point (to the nearest whole unit).
questions.explanation: Each item contributes 65 - 45 = N20 towards the fixed cost, so break-even is where 65x = 25,000 + 45x, giving 20x = 25,000 and x = 1,250 items. Option C divides the fixed cost by the selling price, option B divides it by the variable cost, and option A divides it by 65 + 45 instead of 65 - 45.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A television manufacturer finds that the total cost of producing and selling x television sets is C(x) = 50x^2 + 3000x + 43750. Each set is sold for N6,000. Determine the break-even points.
questions.explanation: Break-even needs R = C, so 6000x = 50x^2 + 3000x + 43750, giving 50x^2 - 3000x + 43750 = 0, and dividing by 50 gives x^2 - 60x + 875 = 0. This factorises as (x - 25)(x - 35) = 0, so x = 25 or x = 35 sets. Option A adds 3000x to the revenue instead of subtracting it, option C is the midpoint where profit is greatest rather than zero, and option B comes from a sign slip when factorising.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company sells its product at N60 per unit. Its fixed cost is N18,000 and the variable cost is estimated to be 25% of total revenue. Find the break-even point.
questions.explanation: Revenue is R = 60x and the variable cost is 25% of revenue, 0.25 x 60x = 15x, so C = 18,000 + 15x. At break-even 60x = 18,000 + 15x, so 45x = 18,000 and x = 400 units. Option D divides the fixed cost by the price alone, ignoring the variable cost, option A divides it by the variable cost per unit, and option C divides by 60 + 15 instead of 60 - 15.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company finds that the fixed cost of a new product is N35,000 and the variable cost per unit is N500. The revenue from selling x units is R(x) = 5000x - 100x^2. Find the break-even values of x (to the nearest whole unit where necessary).
questions.explanation: Profit is P(x) = R - C = 5000x - 100x^2 - (35,000 + 500x) = 4500x - 100x^2 - 35,000. Setting P(x) = 0 and dividing by -100 gives x^2 - 45x + 350 = 0, so (x - 10)(x - 35) = 0 and x = 10 or x = 35. Option A forgets the variable cost of N500 per unit, option D adds it instead of subtracting it, and option C is a sign slip in the factorisation.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company finds that the fixed cost of a new product is N35,000 and the variable cost per unit is N500. The revenue from selling x units is R(x) = 5000x - 100x^2. For which values of x does the company make a loss?
questions.explanation: Profit is P(x) = 4500x - 100x^2 - 35,000 = -100(x - 10)(x - 35), which is zero at x = 10 and x = 35. Because the x^2 coefficient is negative, P(x) is positive between the roots and negative outside them; for example P(5) = -15,000, P(20) = +15,000 and P(40) = -15,000. So a loss occurs for 0 <= x < 10 or x > 35; option D is the profit region, and options C and B each give only one of the two loss regions.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand function for a monopolist is x = 100 - 4p, where x is the number of units produced and sold and p is the price per unit. Which of these is the total revenue function in terms of x?
questions.explanation: Total revenue is price times quantity, so first make p the subject: 4p = 100 - x gives p = 25 - x/4, and R = px = 25x - x^2/4. Option C is the average revenue (the price itself), not total revenue, and option A treats the demand equation as if it were p = 100 - 4x.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm knows that the demand function for one of its products is linear. It can sell 1000 units when the price is N4 per unit and 1500 units when the price is N2 per unit. Find the demand function, where x is the quantity demanded and p is the price.
questions.explanation: The slope is (1500 - 1000)/(2 - 4) = -250 units per naira, so x - 1000 = -250(p - 4), which gives x = 2000 - 250p; check: p = 4 gives 1000 and p = 2 gives 1500. Option D loses the minus sign (demand falls as price rises), and option C uses the first quantity as the intercept without adjusting for the price of N4.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company wants to launch a new product. The fixed cost is N7,500 and the variable cost is N500 per unit. The revenue received on the sale of x units is R = 2500x - 100x^2. Find the break-even points (to 2 decimal places where necessary).
questions.explanation: Profit is P = R - C = 2500x - 100x^2 - (7500 + 500x) = 2000x - 100x^2 - 7500. Break-even means P = 0, so x^2 - 20x + 75 = 0, i.e. (x - 5)(x - 15) = 0, giving x = 5 and x = 15 units. Option D is where profit is greatest, not where it is zero, and option A leaves out the N500 variable cost per unit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company paid N16,100 towards rent of the building and interest on a loan. The cost of producing one unit of a product is N20, and each unit is sold for N27. Find the break-even point (to the nearest whole unit).
questions.explanation: At break-even, revenue equals total cost: 27x = 16,100 + 20x, so 7x = 16,100 and x = 2,300 units. Each unit contributes N27 - N20 = N7 towards the fixed N16,100. Option A divides the fixed cost by the unit cost instead of the contribution per unit, and option C divides by the selling price, ignoring the N20 cost of each unit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company has a fixed cost of N26,000, and the cost of producing one unit is N30. If each unit sells for N43, find the break-even point (to the nearest whole unit).
questions.explanation: Break-even is where the contribution from sales just covers the fixed cost. Each unit contributes 43 - 30 = N13, so x = 26,000/13 = 2,000 units (check: 43(2000) = 86,000 = 26,000 + 30(2000)). Option A divides by the selling price only, and option C divides by the unit cost; neither uses the contribution per unit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company sells its product for N10 per unit. Fixed costs are N35,000 and variable costs are estimated at 30% of total revenue. How many units must the company sell to cover its fixed cost, that is, to break even (to the nearest whole unit)?
questions.explanation: Revenue is R = 10x and variable cost is 30% of that, 3x, so C = 3x + 35,000. Breaking even needs 10x = 3x + 35,000, so 7x = 35,000 and x = 5,000 units. Option A ignores the variable cost and only matches revenue to the fixed cost, and option C divides the fixed cost by the variable cost per unit instead of the N7 contribution.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The fixed cost of a new product is N30,000 and the variable cost per unit is N800. If the demand function is p(x) = 4500 - 100x, find the break-even values of x (to 2 decimal places where necessary).
questions.explanation: Revenue is R = px = 4500x - 100x^2 and cost is C = 30,000 + 800x. Setting R = C gives 100x^2 - 3700x + 30,000 = 0, i.e. x^2 - 37x + 300 = (x - 12)(x - 25) = 0, so the break-even values are x = 12 and x = 25. Option D is the midpoint, where profit is highest, and option A leaves out the N800 variable cost.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand function of a product is D = 10p/(p - 3) and the supply function is S = p^2, where p is the price per unit in naira. Using set theory (the intersection of the demand and supply sets), determine the equilibrium price and quantity.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium demand equals supply, so 10p/(p - 3) = p^2, which gives 10p = p^3 - 3p^2, i.e. p(p - 5)(p + 2) = 0; rejecting p = 0 and p = -2, the price is p = N5 and the quantity is 5^2 = 10(5)/(5 - 3) = 25 units. Equivalently, the sets {(p, D)} and {(p, S)} have the single common pair (5, 25) for prices above N3. Option D lies on the demand curve only, since supply at N4 is just 16 units, and option A lies on the supply curve only, since demand at N6 is 20 units.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand function for a product is D = (5p - 2)/(p - 3) and the supply function is S = p^2 + 2, where p is the price in naira per unit. Find the equilibrium price and quantity.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium D = S, so 5p - 2 = (p^2 + 2)(p - 3) = p^3 - 3p^2 + 2p - 6, which simplifies to p^3 - 3p^2 - 3p - 4 = 0 = (p - 4)(p^2 + p + 1). Since p^2 + p + 1 has no real roots, p = 4 and Q = 4^2 + 2 = 18 (check: D = 18/1 = 18). Option B forgets the +2 in the supply function, option D uses p = 3, where demand is undefined, and at p = 5 (option C) demand is only 11.5 while supply is 27.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The weekly demand and supply functions for bags of cement in a Lagos market are Qd = 120 - 4P and Qs = 6P - 30, where Q is in hundreds of bags and P is the price in thousands of naira. What is the equilibrium price of a bag of cement?
questions.explanation: At equilibrium Qd = Qs, so 120 - 4P = 6P - 30, giving 10P = 150 and P = 15, that is N15,000 per bag. Option A comes from writing 120 - 30 instead of 120 + 30 when collecting the constants, and option C is the equilibrium quantity (60 hundred bags) read as a price.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The daily demand and supply functions for loaves of bread from a bakery are Qd = 2,400 - 30P and Qs = 600 + 15P, where P is the price in naira. Find the equilibrium quantity.
questions.explanation: Setting 2,400 - 30P = 600 + 15P gives 45P = 1,800, so P = N40 and Q = 2,400 - 30(40) = 1,200 loaves (check: 600 + 15(40) = 1,200). Option D is just 2,400 - 600, which stops before solving for P, while options C and B come from dividing 1,800 by 30 only (P = 60), which makes demand and supply disagree.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand function for a product is Qd = 200 - 5P and its supply function is Qs = a + 3P, where a is a constant. If the market is in equilibrium at a price of N20, what is the value of a?
questions.explanation: At P = 20 the quantity demanded is 200 - 5(20) = 100, and supply must equal this at equilibrium: a + 3(20) = 100, so a = 40. Option A is the equilibrium quantity itself, and option D comes from adding 3P to 100 instead of subtracting it.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Producers of a snack are willing to supply 100 packs when the price is N40 per pack and 180 packs when the price is N60 per pack. Assuming the supply function is linear, Qs = c + dP, which of the following is the supply function?
questions.explanation: The slope is d = (180 - 100)/(60 - 40) = 80/20 = 4, and substituting the first point gives 100 = c + 4(40), so c = -60 and Qs = 4P - 60 (check: 4(60) - 60 = 180). Option A uses the change in price over the change in quantity (20/80 = 0.25), which is the slope of P against Q, and option C has the wrong sign on the intercept.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply functions for a product are Qd = 90 - 2P and Qs = 3P - 10. If the price is fixed at N15, what is the excess demand?
questions.explanation: At P = 15, Qd = 90 - 2(15) = 60 and Qs = 3(15) - 10 = 35, so excess demand = Qd - Qs = 60 - 35 = 25 units, a shortage, since N15 is below the equilibrium price of N20. Option B subtracts the wrong way round (Qs - Qd), and option A adds the two quantities instead of finding their difference.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply functions for a product are P = 600 - 2q and P = 120 + 4q respectively, where P is the price in naira and q is the quantity in units. Find the excess supply when the price is N500.
questions.explanation: At P = 500, demand gives 500 = 600 - 2q, so qd = 50, and supply gives 500 = 120 + 4q, so qs = 95. Excess supply = qs - qd = 95 - 50 = 45 units, which fits the fact that N500 is above the equilibrium price of N440. Option B compares quantity supplied with the equilibrium quantity of 80 instead of with quantity demanded, and option C has the subtraction reversed.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: In a market with a downward-sloping demand curve and an upward-sloping supply curve, excess demand (a shortage) occurs when

options.a: quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded
options.b: the market price is equal to the equilibrium price
options.c: the market price is below the equilibrium price
options.d: the market price is above the equilibrium price

questions.explanation: Below the equilibrium price, buyers want more than sellers are willing to offer, so Qd - Qs is positive and the shortage pushes the price back up towards equilibrium. Option D describes the opposite case, where a surplus appears, and option A is the definition of excess supply, not excess demand.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply functions for a product are Qd = 100 - 2P and Qs = 2P - 20. The government imposes a tax of N4 per unit on producers, so that producers receive (P - 4) for each unit sold at market price P. What is the new equilibrium market price?
questions.explanation: With the tax, supply becomes Qs = 2(P - 4) - 20 = 2P - 28, and setting 100 - 2P = 2P - 28 gives 4P = 128, so P = N32 (up from N30 before the tax). Option D assumes the whole N4 is passed on to consumers, but with these slopes the price rises by only N2. Option B comes from writing (P + 4) instead of (P - 4), which treats the tax like a subsidy.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply functions for a product are Qd = 120 - 3P and Qs = 2P - 30. A tax of N5 per unit is imposed on producers, so that producers receive (P - 5) for each unit sold at market price P. How much tax revenue does the government collect at the new equilibrium?
questions.explanation: After the tax, supply is Qs = 2(P - 5) - 30 = 2P - 40, so 120 - 3P = 2P - 40 gives P = N32 and Q = 120 - 3(32) = 24 units. Tax revenue = tax per unit x quantity sold = 5 x 24 = N120. Option D uses the pre-tax quantity of 30, but the tax itself reduces the quantity traded, and option B multiplies the tax by the price instead of the quantity.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply functions for a product are Qd = 180 - 4P and Qs = 2P - 30. A tax of N6 per unit is imposed on producers, so that producers receive (P - 6) for each unit sold at market price P. After the tax, what price per unit do producers actually keep?
questions.explanation: The new supply is Qs = 2(P - 6) - 30 = 2P - 42, so 180 - 4P = 2P - 42 gives 6P = 222 and a market price of N37. Producers pass N6 of this to the government and keep 37 - 6 = N31. Option A is the price consumers pay, not what producers keep, and option C assumes producers absorb the whole tax from the old equilibrium price of N35.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply functions for bags of fertiliser are Qd = 150 - 3P and Qs = 3P + 30, where P is in thousands of naira. The government pays producers a subsidy of N6 thousand per bag, so that producers receive (P + 6) for each bag sold at market price P. What is the new equilibrium market price?
questions.explanation: With the subsidy, supply becomes Qs = 3(P + 6) + 30 = 3P + 48, and 150 - 3P = 3P + 48 gives 6P = 102, so P = 17, that is N17 thousand (down from N20 thousand). Option C assumes buyers get the whole N6 thousand reduction, but here they get only half of it, and option B treats the subsidy as a tax by writing (P - 6).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply functions for a product are P = 90 - 2Q and P = 30 + Q. The government gives producers a subsidy of N6 per unit, which shifts the supply function to P = 24 + Q. What is the total cost of the subsidy to the government at the new equilibrium?
questions.explanation: With the subsidy, 90 - 2Q = 24 + Q gives 3Q = 66, so Q = 22 units, and the government pays 6 x 22 = N132. Option B uses the old equilibrium quantity of 20, forgetting that the subsidy increases the quantity traded, and option C multiplies the subsidy by the new price (N46) instead of the quantity.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A per-unit tax is imposed on the producers of a good whose demand curve slopes downward and whose supply curve slopes upward. Which of the following best describes the effect on the market equilibrium?

options.a: The price paid by consumers rises by less than the tax and the quantity traded falls
options.b: The price paid by consumers falls and the quantity traded rises
options.c: Price and quantity are unchanged because only producers pay the tax
options.d: The price paid by consumers rises by the full amount of the tax and the quantity is unchanged

questions.explanation: A per-unit tax on producers shifts the supply curve up by the amount of the tax, so the new equilibrium has a higher price and a smaller quantity. Because buyers respond to the higher price by buying less, only part of the tax is passed on and the price rises by less than the tax. Option D would hold only if quantity demanded did not respond to price at all, and option C ignores the fact that the tax raises producers' costs.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand function for a brand of rice is Q = 500 - 25P + 0.02Y + 6Pr, where P is its price, Y is consumers' income and Pr is the price of a related good. Calculate Q when P = 12, Y = 50,000 and Pr = 15.
questions.explanation: Substituting gives Q = 500 - 25(12) + 0.02(50,000) + 6(15) = 500 - 300 + 1,000 + 90 = 1,290. Option C adds the price term instead of subtracting it, and options D and B each drop one term (the related-good term and the income term respectively).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A demand function is Q = 200 - 4P + 0.01Y + 2T, where P is the price in naira, Y is income and T is an index of taste. If Y = 30,000 and T = 10, at what price will the quantity demanded be 260 units?
questions.explanation: First evaluate the other terms: 200 + 0.01(30,000) + 2(10) = 200 + 300 + 20 = 520, so 520 - 4P = 260, 4P = 260 and P = N65. Option B leaves out the taste term 2T = 20, and option C adds 260 to 520 instead of subtracting it.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand for a product is Q = 800 - 10P + 0.04Y - 2Pr, where P is its price, Y is income and Pr is the price of a related good. If income rises by N5,000 while P and Pr stay the same, what happens to the quantity demanded?
questions.explanation: Only the income term changes, so the change in Q is 0.04 x 5,000 = 200, and because the coefficient of Y is positive the quantity demanded rises by 200 units. Option D has the right size but the wrong direction, and options A and C are decimal-place slips (0.4 or 0.004 used instead of 0.04).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: In the demand function Q = 900 - 15P + 0.05Y + 8Pr, where Pr is the price of a related good, the positive coefficient of Pr shows that the two goods are
questions.explanation: A positive coefficient means that when the price of the related good rises, demand for this good also rises, which happens when buyers switch from one good to the other, so the goods are substitutes. Complements (option C) would have a negative coefficient, because a dearer related good reduces demand for both. Inferior goods (option B) describe how demand responds to income, not to another good's price.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm producing 2,500 units of output incurs a total cost of N450,000, of which N150,000 is fixed cost. What is its average variable cost?
questions.explanation: Variable cost = total cost - fixed cost = 450,000 - 150,000 = N300,000, so AVC = 300,000/2,500 = N120 per unit. Option D is the average total cost (450,000/2,500), and option C is the average fixed cost (150,000/2,500).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: At an output of 400 units, a firm's average fixed cost is N25 and its average variable cost is N75. What is its total cost?
questions.explanation: Average total cost = AFC + AVC = 25 + 75 = N100 per unit, so total cost = 100 x 400 = N40,000. Option B stops at the average total cost, and option A is only the total variable cost (75 x 400), leaving out the fixed cost of 25 x 400 = N10,000.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm's total cost is linear in output. It costs N51,000 to produce 300 units and N75,000 to produce 500 units. What is the firm's fixed cost?
questions.explanation: The extra 200 units add 75,000 - 51,000 = N24,000, so the variable cost is 24,000/200 = N120 per unit. Then fixed cost = 51,000 - 120(300) = N15,000 (check: 15,000 + 120(500) = 75,000). Option A is the change in total cost, not the fixed cost, and option D wrongly treats 75,000/500 = N150 as the variable cost per unit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm's total cost function is TC(Q) = 2Q^3 - 12Q^2 + 60Q + 900. Find the average variable cost when Q = 5.
questions.explanation: The fixed cost is TC(0) = 900, so VC = 2Q^3 - 12Q^2 + 60Q and AVC = VC/Q = 2Q^2 - 12Q + 60. At Q = 5, AVC = 2(25) - 12(5) + 60 = 50. Option A is the average total cost, which adds AFC = 900/5 = 180 (option B), and option D is the marginal cost 6Q^2 - 24Q + 60 at Q = 5.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The total cost (in naira) of producing x units of a product is C(x) = 5,000 + 40x + 0.5x^2. Find the total cost of producing 60 units.
questions.explanation: C(60) = 5,000 + 40(60) + 0.5(60)^2 = 5,000 + 2,400 + 1,800 = N9,200. Option C is only the variable part (2,400 + 1,800), leaving out the fixed cost of N5,000, and option A squares 0.5 x 60 = 30 instead of multiplying 0.5 by 60^2.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The total cost (in naira) of producing x units is C(x) = 2,000 + 15x + 0.1x^2. By how much does total cost increase when output rises from 50 units to 60 units?
questions.explanation: C(60) = 2,000 + 900 + 360 = N3,260 and C(50) = 2,000 + 750 + 250 = N3,000, so the increase is 3,260 - 3,000 = N260. Option D is the total cost at 60 units, not the increase, and option C counts only the linear part 15 x 10 and ignores the change in the 0.1x^2 term.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A bakery in Yaba has monthly fixed costs of N350,000 and a variable cost of N180 per loaf. If its total cost for a month was N1,070,000, how many loaves did it produce (to the nearest loaf)?
questions.explanation: Total cost = fixed cost + variable cost, so 350,000 + 180x = 1,070,000, giving 180x = 720,000 and x = 4,000 loaves. Option A divides the whole total cost by N180, as if there were no fixed cost, and option C adds the fixed cost instead of subtracting it.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand function for a product is p = 400 - 0.5x, where p is the price in naira and x is the number of units sold. Find the total revenue when 300 units are sold.
questions.explanation: At x = 300 the price is p = 400 - 0.5(300) = N250, so revenue R = px = 250 x 300 = N75,000. Option D multiplies 300 by the intercept 400 and ignores the fall in price, while option A is the price per unit, not the revenue.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm's demand function is p = 120 - 2x and its total cost function is C(x) = 300 + 20x, where x is the number of units and amounts are in naira. What is the profit when 20 units are produced and sold?
questions.explanation: Revenue is R(20) = 20(120 - 2(20)) = 20 x 80 = N1,600 and cost is C(20) = 300 + 20(20) = N700, so profit P = R - C = 1,600 - 700 = N900. Option D subtracts only the fixed cost, and option B adds the fixed cost instead of subtracting it.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm has fixed costs of N50,000 and a variable cost of N35 per unit. What selling price per unit will make it break even at an output of 2,000 units?
questions.explanation: At break-even, revenue = cost: 2,000p = 50,000 + 35(2,000), so 2,000p = 120,000 and p = N60. Option B spreads only the fixed cost over the 2,000 units and forgets that each unit must also cover its own N35 variable cost, while option D covers the variable cost but none of the fixed cost.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm's revenue function is R(x) = 500x - x^2 and its cost function is C(x) = 20,000 + 100x, both in naira. Find the profit when 150 units are produced and sold.
questions.explanation: R(150) = 500(150) - 150^2 = 75,000 - 22,500 = N52,500 and C(150) = 20,000 + 100(150) = N35,000, so profit = 52,500 - 35,000 = N17,500. Option D is the revenue, not the profit, and option A forgets to subtract the N20,000 fixed cost.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A small printing shop in Lagos prints branded T-shirts. Its fixed costs are N240,000, the variable cost is N900 per shirt and each shirt sells for N1,500. How many shirts must it sell to break even (to the nearest shirt)?
questions.explanation: Each shirt contributes 1,500 - 900 = N600 towards fixed costs, so break-even quantity = F/(p - v) = 240,000/600 = 400 shirts. Option A divides by the selling price only (240,000/1,500), and option C divides by the variable cost (240,000/900, about 267).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm has fixed costs of N90,000. Its product sells for N50 per unit and the variable cost is N30 per unit. What is the break-even sales revenue?
questions.explanation: The break-even quantity is 90,000/(50 - 30) = 4,500 units, so break-even revenue = 50 x 4,500 = N225,000 (equivalently, 90,000 divided by the contribution ratio 20/50 = 0.4). Option D divides by the variable cost ratio 0.6 instead of the contribution ratio, and option A values the break-even units at the variable cost of N30 instead of the selling price.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm sells its product at N25 per unit, has fixed costs of N60,000 and a variable cost of N15 per unit. If the variable cost per unit falls to N13, with price and fixed costs unchanged, what is the new break-even quantity (to the nearest unit)?
questions.explanation: The contribution per unit rises from 25 - 15 = N10 to 25 - 13 = N12, so the new break-even quantity is 60,000/12 = 5,000 units, down from 6,000. Option C is the old break-even point, and option B adds N2 to the variable cost instead of subtracting it.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm's demand function is p = 200 - 2x and its total cost function is C(x) = 1,400 + 40x, where x is the number of units and amounts are in naira. Find the break-even quantities (to 2 decimal places where necessary).
questions.explanation: Revenue is R = x(200 - 2x) = 200x - 2x^2, so profit is P = 200x - 2x^2 - 1,400 - 40x = -2(x^2 - 80x + 700) = -2(x - 10)(x - 70), which is zero at x = 10 and x = 70. Option D is the output that maximises profit (midway between the two roots), not a break-even point, and option B comes from leaving out the variable cost 40x.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A product sells for N800 per unit and its variable cost is N520 per unit. What is its contribution margin ratio (contribution per unit as a percentage of the selling price)?
questions.explanation: Contribution per unit is 800 - 520 = N280, and as a share of the selling price this is 280/800 = 0.35, or 35%. Option B is the variable cost ratio (520/800), which is the part of each naira of sales that is not contribution, and option D wrongly divides the contribution by the variable cost instead of the price.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A company sells 1,500 units of a product at N1,200 each. The variable cost is N750 per unit and fixed costs are N540,000. What is the total contribution?
questions.explanation: Total contribution = (selling price - variable cost per unit) x units = (1,200 - 750) x 1,500 = 450 x 1,500 = N675,000. Option B goes one step further and subtracts the fixed costs, which gives profit rather than contribution, while option D is the total variable cost.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm's contribution margin ratio is 40% and its fixed costs are N120,000. What sales revenue must it achieve to earn a profit of N30,000?
questions.explanation: Contribution must cover both the fixed costs and the target profit, so 0.40 x Sales = 120,000 + 30,000 = 150,000, giving Sales = 150,000/0.40 = N375,000. Option C is only the break-even revenue (120,000/0.40), which gives zero profit, and option D divides by the variable cost ratio of 0.60 instead of the contribution ratio.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm has fixed costs of N72,000, sells its product at N40 per unit and has a variable cost of N22 per unit. If it currently sells 5,000 units, what is its margin of safety in units (actual sales minus break-even sales), to the nearest unit?
questions.explanation: Break-even quantity = 72,000/(40 - 22) = 72,000/18 = 4,000 units, so the margin of safety = 5,000 - 4,000 = 1,000 units: sales can fall by 1,000 units before the firm makes a loss. Option C is the break-even quantity itself, and option A uses 72,000/40 as the break-even point, forgetting to subtract the variable cost from the price.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: A firm's budgeted sales are N500,000 and its break-even sales are N350,000. What is its margin of safety as a percentage of budgeted sales (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Margin of safety = 500,000 - 350,000 = N150,000, and as a percentage of budgeted sales this is 150,000/500,000 x 100 = 30%. Option C divides by break-even sales instead of budgeted sales, and option A is break-even sales as a share of budgeted sales, the part of sales needed just to avoid a loss.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand function for a product is Q = 200 - 4P. Using the price elasticity of demand E = -(P/Q)(dQ/dP), find E when P = 20 (correct to 2 decimal places) and describe the demand.
questions.explanation: At P = 20, Q = 200 - 4(20) = 120 and dQ/dP = -4, so E = -(20/120)(-4) = 80/120 = 0.67. Since 0.67 lies between 0 and 1, demand is inelastic at this price. Option C turns the answer upside down (120/80 = 1.50), and option A is the slope alone, which ignores the price and quantity at the point.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The inverse demand function for a product is P = 60 - 2Q. Using E = -(P/Q)(dQ/dP), find the price elasticity of demand when Q = 10.
questions.explanation: At Q = 10, P = 60 - 2(10) = 40. From P = 60 - 2Q, dP/dQ = -2, so dQ/dP = -1/2 and E = -(40/10)(-1/2) = 2, meaning demand is elastic at this point. Option B multiplies by dP/dQ = -2 in place of dQ/dP, and option D is P/Q without the slope.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: When the price of garri rises by 10%, the quantity demanded falls by 4%. What is the price elasticity of demand (in absolute value), and how is the demand described?
questions.explanation: Elasticity = percentage change in quantity demanded / percentage change in price = 4%/10% = 0.4. A value between 0 and 1 means demand is inelastic: buyers cut purchases by proportionally less than the price rise. Option A divides the wrong way round (10/4 = 2.5), and option B has the right number but the wrong description.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The demand and supply functions for a product are Qd = 90 - 3P and Qs = 2P - 10. Using E = -(P/Q)(dQd/dP) for the demand function, what is the price elasticity of demand at the equilibrium point (to 2 decimal places where necessary)?
questions.explanation: At equilibrium 90 - 3P = 2P - 10, so P = 20 and Q = 30. Using the demand slope dQd/dP = -3, E = -(20/30)(-3) = 2, so demand is elastic there. Option A uses the supply slope of 2 instead of the demand slope, and option B is the reciprocal of the correct value (1/2 instead of 2).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: As a firm's output increases, its average fixed cost (AFC)

options.a: falls continuously, because the same fixed cost is spread over more units
options.b: stays the same at every level of output
options.c: first falls and then rises, giving a U-shaped curve
options.d: rises, because fixed cost increases as more units are produced

questions.explanation: AFC = FC/Q, and since fixed cost does not change with output, dividing it by a larger Q always gives a smaller figure, so AFC keeps falling. Option D confuses fixed cost with variable cost, and option C describes the usual shape of average variable or average total cost, not AFC.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Which of the following cost relationships is NOT correct? (TC = total cost, FC = fixed cost, VC = variable cost, Q = output)
questions.explanation: Average variable cost divides only the variable cost by output, AVC = VC/Q = (TC - FC)/Q, so TC/Q is the average total cost, not AVC. The other three are standard identities: VC = TC - FC (option D), AFC = FC/Q (option A) and ATC = AFC + AVC (option C).

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a fixed cost for a sachet-water factory?

options.a: Wages paid to workers per bag of water produced
options.b: Cost of the nylon sachets used for packaging
options.c: Cost of the purification chemicals used per 1,000 litres
options.d: Annual rent on the factory building

questions.explanation: A fixed cost stays the same whatever the level of production, and rent on the premises must be paid even if no sachet is produced. Packaging sachets (option B), wages paid per bag (option A) and treatment chemicals (option C) all rise with the number of units produced, so they are variable costs.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true at a firm's break-even point?

options.b: Total revenue equals total variable cost

questions.explanation: At break-even R(x) = C(x), so profit is zero and the total contribution (revenue minus variable cost) is exactly enough to cover fixed cost. Revenue therefore exceeds variable cost by the amount of the fixed cost, so it cannot equal variable cost unless there are no fixed costs. Option C may look unfamiliar, but it is just another way of writing R - VC = FC.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: If F is fixed cost, p is the selling price per unit and v is the variable cost per unit, the break-even quantity is given by
questions.explanation: At break-even pq = F + vq, so (p - v)q = F and q = F/(p - v), the fixed cost divided by the contribution per unit. Option D is the formula turned upside down, and option A ignores the variable cost that each unit also has to cover.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: In break-even analysis, the contribution margin per unit is

options.a: fixed cost divided by the number of units sold
options.b: selling price per unit minus total cost per unit
options.d: selling price per unit minus variable cost per unit

questions.explanation: Contribution per unit, p - v, is what each unit sold contributes first towards covering fixed costs and then towards profit. Option B gives profit per unit, because total cost per unit already includes a share of fixed cost, and option A is the average fixed cost.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: The margin of safety of a firm measures

options.a: the amount by which fixed costs exceed variable costs
options.b: the level of output at which total revenue equals total cost
options.c: the profit the firm earns on each unit sold
options.d: how far actual or budgeted sales can fall before the firm starts to make a loss

questions.explanation: Margin of safety = actual (or budgeted) sales - break-even sales, so it shows the cushion of sales the firm can lose before profit turns into a loss. Option B describes the break-even point itself, and option C describes profit per unit.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: Demand whose elasticity coefficient (in absolute value) is greater than 1 is described as
questions.explanation: When the coefficient exceeds 1, the percentage change in quantity demanded is larger than the percentage change in price, so demand is relatively elastic. Relatively inelastic demand (option B) has a coefficient between 0 and 1, unitary elasticity (option A) has a coefficient of exactly 1, and perfectly inelastic demand (option D) has a coefficient of 0.

questions.topic: Demand, Supply, Cost, Revenue and Break-even
questions.question: If the demand for a product is inelastic at its current price, a small increase in price will
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand the percentage fall in quantity is smaller than the percentage rise in price, so price times quantity goes up and total revenue increases. Option A is what happens when demand is elastic, and option C happens only at unit elasticity.

questions.question: A principal of N5,000 is invested at 6% interest. Find the amount after 10 years if the interest is compounded daily.
questions.explanation: With daily compounding, A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) = 5,000(1 + 0.06/365)^(365 x 10) = 5,000 x 1.822029 = N9,110.14. Even continuous compounding, the fastest possible growth at 6%, gives only about N9,110.59, so options A, C and D are far too large.

questions.question: A principal of N2,500 is invested at 2% interest. Find the amount after 20 years if the interest is compounded monthly.
questions.explanation: Monthly compounding gives A = 2,500(1 + 0.02/12)^(12 x 20) = 2,500 x 1.491328 = N3,728.32, or N3,728 to the nearest naira. Even continuous compounding at 2% gives only about N3,729.56, so options A, C and D are all too large; C, N3,827, simply swaps two digits of the correct answer.

questions.question: The price of gold falls by 34% in the first six months of a year and rises by 12% in the last six months. Work out the overall percentage decrease during the year. Round your answer to the nearest unit.
questions.explanation: Successive percentage changes multiply: after a 34% fall the price is 0.66 of its original, and a 12% rise then gives 0.66 x 1.12 = 0.7392. The overall change is 1 - 0.7392 = 0.2608, a decrease of about 26%. Option C, 22%, comes from simply subtracting 34 - 12, which ignores that the 12% rise is applied to a smaller price.

questions.question: A regular sum of N2,500 is invested at the beginning of every year at 3.5% interest compounded annually. Find the total amount invested at the end of 10 years.
questions.explanation: Payments at the start of each year form an annuity due, so each payment earns one extra year of interest: FV = 2,500 x [(1.035^10 - 1)/0.035] x 1.035 = 2,500 x 11.731393 x 1.035 = N30,354.98.
