questions.explanation: The scale factors are 0.60 and 1.50, and 0.60 x 1.50 = 0.90, which is a 10% decrease overall. Option D just adds -40% and +50%, ignoring that the 50% rise is applied to a much lower price. Option C assumes the rise recovers the fall, but a rise of about 66.67% would be needed for that.

questions.question: After falling by 20%, by what percentage must a price rise to return to its original level? Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: After the fall the price is 0.8 of the original, so it must be multiplied by 1/0.8 = 1.25, which is a 25% rise. Option A forgets that the 20% rise would be applied to the smaller, reduced price. Option D is the fall needed to undo a 20% rise (1 - 1/1.2), the reverse situation, and option B is the fraction of the price left after the fall.

questions.question: A trader buys 50 crates of eggs at N4,800 per crate. Five crates break, and she sells the rest at N6,000 per crate. What is her percentage profit on cost price?
questions.explanation: Total cost = 50 x 4,800 = N240,000 and sales = 45 x 6,000 = N270,000, so profit = N30,000 and percentage profit = 30,000/240,000 x 100 = 12.5%. Option A is the profit per crate sold (1,200/4,800) and ignores the broken crates. Option B divides the profit by the selling price instead of the cost price.

questions.question: A trader sold a generator for N171,000 at a loss of 5%. What was the cost price of the generator?
questions.explanation: Selling at a 5% loss means SP = 0.95 x CP, so CP = 171,000/0.95 = N180,000. Option B adds 5% of the selling price, but the loss is 5% of the cost price, not of the selling price. Option D takes a further 5% off, and option A divides by 1.05 as if the trader had made a profit.

questions.question: A shop gives a 20% discount on a television and then a further 10% discount on the reduced price. What single discount is equivalent to the two discounts?
questions.explanation: The customer pays 0.80 x 0.90 = 0.72 of the original price, so the single equivalent discount is 1 - 0.72 = 28%. Option C simply adds 20% and 10%, but the second discount is taken from the already reduced price. Option A is the fraction of the price still paid, not the discount, and option D is only the overlap term 20 x 10/100.

questions.question: Find the value of cofactors A11 of the matrix [[2,4,1],[4,3,7],[2,1,3]]
questions.explanation: The cofactor A11 = (-1)^(1+1) x M11, where the minor M11 is the determinant left after deleting row 1 and column 1, [[3,7],[1,3]], so M11 = 3(3) - 7(1) = 9 - 7 = 2. The sign (-1)^2 = +1, so A11 = 2. Option A, 6, is the cofactor A23 of this matrix, not A11.

questions.question: Find the determinants of A = [[1,3,3],[1,4,3],[1,3,4]]
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row: |A| = 1(4x4 - 3x3) - 3(1x4 - 3x1) + 3(1x3 - 4x1) = 1(7) - 3(1) + 3(-1) = 7 - 3 - 3 = 1. Option B, 7, is only the first term of the expansion; the middle term carries a minus sign and all three terms must be combined.

questions.question: Find the determinants of B = [[270,-372,0],[552,201,0],[999,413,0]]
questions.explanation: Every entry in the third column of B is 0, and any determinant with a whole row or column of zeros equals 0. You can see this by expanding down the third column: each term is 0 multiplied by a cofactor. The large entries tempt a long calculation, but options A, B and D cannot be right.

questions.question: Find all the cofactors of the matrix A = [[2,4,1],[4,3,7],[2,1,3]]. Which matrix lists the cofactor C_ij in row i, column j?
questions.explanation: Each cofactor is C_ij = (-1)^(i+j) M_ij, where the minor M_ij is the determinant left after deleting row i and column j; for example C11 = 3(3) - 7(1) = 2, C12 = -(4(3) - 7(2)) = 2 and C21 = -(4(3) - 1(1)) = -11. As a check, expanding along row 1 gives 2(2) + 4(2) + 1(-2) = 10 = |A|. Option B lists the minors without the alternating signs, Option C is the transpose of the cofactor matrix (the adjoint), and Option D has every sign reversed.

questions.question: Find the determinants of A = [[1,3,3],[1,4,3],[1,3,4]] and B = [[270,-372,0],[552,201,0],[999,413,0]].
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row, |A| = 1(4(4) - 3(3)) - 3(1(4) - 3(1)) + 3(1(3) - 4(1)) = 7 - 3 - 3 = 1. Matrix B has a whole column of zeros, so every term of its expansion contains a zero and |B| = 0. Option A keeps only the first term of the expansion of |A|, and Option C wrongly evaluates just the non-zero 2 x 2 block of B (270 x 201 + 372 x 552 = 259,614).

questions.question: Find the inverse of the matrix A = [[1,2,-3],[2,-1,4],[4,3,-4]] (for example, by reducing [A | I] to row canonical form).
questions.explanation: Here |A| = 1(4 - 12) - 2(-8 - 16) + (-3)(6 + 4) = -8 + 48 - 30 = 10, and row-reducing [A | I] (or using adj A/|A|) gives A^-1 = (1/10)[[-8,-1,5],[24,8,-10],[10,5,-5]], that is [[-4/5,-1/10,1/2],[12/5,4/5,-1],[1,1/2,-1/2]]. You can check that A times this matrix gives I. Option A is the cofactor matrix divided by 10 without transposing it, Option D has every sign reversed as if |A| were -10, and Option C forgets to divide by |A|.

questions.question: Let A = [[4,0],[2,1]] and B = [[2,0],[1,2]]. Find (AB)^-1, which by the reversal rule equals B^-1 A^-1.
questions.explanation: First AB = [[4,0],[2,1]][[2,0],[1,2]] = [[8,0],[5,2]], so |AB| = 16 - 0 = 16 and (AB)^-1 = (1/16)[[2,0],[-5,8]] = [[1/8,0],[-5/16,1/2]]. The same matrix comes from B^-1 A^-1 = [[1/2,0],[-1/4,1/2]][[1/4,0],[-1/2,1]], confirming (AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1. Option C is A^-1 B^-1, multiplied in the wrong order, Option A is the adjoint of AB not divided by 16, and Option B forgets to change the sign of the off-diagonal entry.

questions.question: Solve the following system with the help of matrices (X = A^-1 B): x + y + z = 6; 5x - y + 2z = 9; 3x + 6y - 5z = 0.

A manufacturer produces three products P, Q and R, which he sells in two markets. Annual sales volumes are given by the matrix [[10000,2000,18000],[6000,20000,8000]] (rows = Markets 1, 2; columns = Products P, Q, R). The unit sale prices of P, Q and R are N2.50, N1.25 and N1.50 respectively, and their unit costs are N1.80, N1.20 and N0.80. Using matrix multiplication, find the total revenue in each market.
questions.explanation: Multiply the sales matrix by the price vector (2.50, 1.25, 1.50): Market 1 = 10,000(2.50) + 2,000(1.25) + 18,000(1.50) = 25,000 + 2,500 + 27,000 = N54,500 and Market 2 = 6,000(2.50) + 20,000(1.25) + 8,000(1.50) = 15,000 + 25,000 + 12,000 = N52,000. Option A uses the unit-cost vector instead of the prices, so it gives the cost in each market, and Option D is the gross profit in each market. Option B swaps the two markets.

questions.question: A manufacturer produces three products P, Q and R, which he sells in two markets. Annual sales volumes are given by the matrix [[10000,2000,18000],[6000,20000,8000]] (rows = Markets 1, 2; columns = Products P, Q, R). The unit sale prices of P, Q and R are N2.50, N1.25 and N1.50 respectively, and their unit costs are N1.80, N1.20 and N0.80. Using matrix multiplication, find the total gross profit from both markets.
questions.explanation: Profit per unit is (2.50 - 1.80, 1.25 - 1.20, 1.50 - 0.80) = (0.70, 0.05, 0.70), so Market 1 profit = 10,000(0.70) + 2,000(0.05) + 18,000(0.70) = 7,000 + 100 + 12,600 = N19,700 and Market 2 profit = 6,000(0.70) + 20,000(0.05) + 8,000(0.70) = 4,200 + 1,000 + 5,600 = N10,800. Total gross profit = N30,500, which is total revenue N106,500 minus total cost N76,000. Option D is total revenue and Option C is total cost, while Option A is the profit of Market 1 only.

questions.question: What is the difference between the minor and the cofactor of an element a_ij in a determinant?

options.a: The cofactor is the minor multiplied by (-1)^(i+j), so the two are equal when i + j is even and differ only in sign when i + j is odd.
options.b: The minor is the cofactor multiplied by the value of the whole determinant.
options.c: The cofactor is the minor divided by the element a_ij.
options.d: The minor is found by deleting only row i, while the cofactor is found by deleting both row i and column j.

questions.explanation: The minor M_ij is the determinant left after deleting row i and column j, and the cofactor attaches a place sign to it: A_ij = (-1)^(i+j) M_ij. So in a 3x3 determinant the cofactor of a_11 equals M_11, but the cofactor of a_12 is -M_12. Option D is wrong because both the minor and the cofactor come from deleting row i and column j, and Option B and Option C describe relationships that do not exist.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the difference between a matrix and a determinant?

options.a: A determinant can have any number of rows and columns, while a matrix must always be square.
options.b: A matrix and a determinant are the same thing written with different brackets.
options.c: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers with no single value, while a determinant is a single number worked out from a square array.
options.d: A matrix always has a numerical value, while a determinant is only an arrangement of numbers.

questions.explanation: A matrix is just an arrangement of numbers in rows and columns (it can be rectangular, such as 2x3) and has no single value, whereas a determinant is one number calculated from a square array, e.g. |[[2,1],[3,4]]| = 2(4) - 1(3) = 5. Option A reverses the facts, because it is the determinant that needs a square array. Option D also swaps the two ideas, and Option B ignores that one is an array and the other is a number.

questions.question: A square matrix A is called a singular matrix when:

options.a: it has exactly one non-zero element in each row

questions.explanation: A square matrix is singular when its determinant is zero; then adj A/|A| cannot be formed, so A has no inverse. For example, [[2,4],[1,2]] is singular because 2(2) - 4(1) = 0. Option C defines a symmetric matrix, and Option B is not the test, since any non-zero determinant (not just 1) makes a matrix non-singular.

questions.question: For a system of linear equations written as AX = B, what is the augmented matrix?

options.a: A^T: the coefficient matrix with its rows and columns interchanged
options.b: [A | B]: the coefficient matrix A with the column of constants B written as an extra column
options.c: adj A: the transpose of the matrix of cofactors of A
options.d: A^-1 B: the column of solutions of the system

questions.explanation: The augmented matrix places the constants beside the coefficients, so for 2x + y = 5 and x - y = 1 it is [[2,1,5],[1,-1,1]]; row operations are then applied to it when solving by Gauss-Jordan elimination. Option D is the final solution X, not the augmented matrix, Option C is the adjoint used to find an inverse, and Option A is the transpose.

questions.question: What is the difference between the adjoint and the transpose of a square matrix A?

options.a: The adjoint of A is A with its rows and columns interchanged, while the transpose of A is the matrix of cofactors of A.
options.b: The adjoint of A is simply the matrix of cofactors of A, with no transposing involved.
options.c: The adjoint of A is the transpose of the matrix of cofactors of A, while the transpose of A is A itself with its rows and columns interchanged.
options.d: The adjoint and the transpose are the same matrix for every square matrix.

questions.explanation: The transpose A^T just swaps the rows and columns of A, while the adjoint first replaces every element by its cofactor and then transposes that cofactor matrix; for [[a,b],[c,d]] the transpose is [[a,c],[b,d]] but the adjoint is [[d,-b],[-c,a]]. The adjoint is what appears in A^-1 = adj A/|A|. Option A swaps the two definitions, Option B leaves out the transposing step, and the 2x2 example shows Option D is false.

questions.question: Evaluate the determinant |[[1,0,3],[6,5,0],[21,3,7]]|.
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row: 1(5 x 7 - 0 x 3) - 0(6 x 7 - 0 x 21) + 3(6 x 3 - 5 x 21) = 35 + 3(18 - 105) = 35 - 261 = -226. Option A has the overall sign wrong, Option C comes from writing the last minor as 105 - 18 (giving 35 + 261), and Option B forgets to multiply the last minor by its element 3 (35 - 87).

questions.question: Evaluate the determinant |[[1,2,-1,2],[3,0,1,5],[1,-2,0,3],[-2,-4,1,6]]|.
questions.explanation: Use R2 - 3R1, R3 - R1 and R4 + 2R1 to clear the first column; the rows become (1, 2, -1, 2), (0, -6, 4, -1), (0, -4, 1, 1) and (0, 0, -1, 10). The determinant is then 1 x |[[-6,4,-1],[-4,1,1],[0,-1,10]]| = -6(10 + 1) - 4(-40 - 0) + (-1)(4 - 0) = -66 + 160 - 4 = 90. Option D has the sign wrong, and Option B comes from adding the three terms of the 3x3 expansion without the alternating + - + signs (-66 - 160 - 4).

questions.question: Using the Sarrus diagram, find the value of |[[1,2,3],[4,5,0],[2,3,7]]|.
questions.explanation: Sarrus' rule adds the three downward diagonal products and subtracts the three upward ones: (1)(5)(7) + (2)(0)(2) + (3)(4)(3) = 35 + 0 + 36 = 71, and (3)(5)(2) + (1)(0)(3) + (2)(4)(7) = 30 + 0 + 56 = 86. So the value is 71 - 86 = -15. Option D subtracts the wrong way round (86 - 71), and Option B adds the two groups (71 + 86) instead of subtracting.

questions.question: Evaluate the determinant |[[0,1,2,3],[-1,0,1,2],[-2,-1,0,1],[-3,-2,-1,0]]|.
questions.explanation: Subtract each row from the one below it, working from the bottom up: R4 - R3, R3 - R2 and R2 - R1 each give (-1, -1, -1, -1), and these operations do not change the value. The new determinant has identical rows, and any determinant with two equal rows is 0. A value such as Option A, Option B or Option C can only come from an arithmetic slip in a long cofactor expansion.

questions.question: If A = [[4,2],[3,6]] and B = [[3,7],[2,8]], find the determinant of the product AB.
questions.explanation: AB = [[4(3) + 2(2), 4(7) + 2(8)],[3(3) + 6(2), 3(7) + 6(8)]] = [[16,44],[21,69]], so |AB| = 16(69) - 44(21) = 1104 - 924 = 180. This equals |A| x |B| = (24 - 6)(24 - 14) = 18 x 10, showing that the determinant of a product is the product of the determinants. Option C adds the two determinants (18 + 10) and Option B subtracts them.

questions.question: Find the value of the determinant |[[1,a,a^2-bc],[1,b,b^2-ca],[1,c,c^2-ab]]|.

options.a: a^2 + b^2 + c^2 - ab - bc - ca

questions.explanation: Apply C3 -> C3 - (a + b + c)C2 + (ab + bc + ca)C1, which does not change the value; in the first row this gives a^2 - bc - (a + b + c)a + (ab + bc + ca) = 0, and the other two rows also become 0. A determinant with a column of zeros equals 0. Option D is the value of |[[1,a,a^2],[1,b,b^2],[1,c,c^2]]| alone, but the -bc, -ca, -ab part contributes exactly the same amount with the opposite sign, so they cancel.

questions.question: Solve using determinants (Cramer's rule): 2x + 5y = 24; 3x + 8y = 38.
Consider the system x - 3y - 8z = -10; 3x + y - 4z = 0; 2x + 5y + 6z = 13. Using determinants (Cramer's rule), which statement about the system is correct?

options.a: D = 0 and the system is consistent, so it has infinitely many solutions, such as (-1, 3, 0) and (1, 1, 1)
options.b: D is non-zero and the unique solution is (x, y, z) = (-10, 3, 0)
options.c: D = 0 and the equations contradict each other, so the system has no solution
options.d: D is non-zero and the unique solution is (x, y, z) = (-1, 3, 0)

questions.explanation: Here D = 1(6 + 20) - (-3)(18 + 8) + (-8)(15 - 2) = 26 + 78 - 104 = 0, so Cramer's rule cannot give a unique solution, and Dx, Dy and Dz are also 0. The third equation is a combination of the other two (10 x third = 11 x second - 13 x first), so the system is consistent with solutions x = -1 + 2t, y = 3 - 2t, z = t, e.g. (-1, 3, 0) and (1, 1, 1). Option B and Option D wrongly assume D is non-zero (and (-10, 3, 0) does not even satisfy the first equation), while Option C would need the equations to contradict each other.

questions.question: Solve using determinants (Cramer's rule): -x + 3y + 2z = 24; x + z = 6; 5y - z = 8.
questions.explanation: D = |[[-1,3,2],[1,0,1],[0,5,-1]]| = -1(0 - 5) - 3(-1 - 0) + 2(5 - 0) = 5 + 3 + 10 = 18. Replacing each column in turn by (24, 6, 8) gives Dx = -18, Dy = 54 and Dz = 126, so x = -18/18 = -1, y = 54/18 = 3 and z = 126/18 = 7; check: -(-1) + 3(3) + 2(7) = 24. Option C drops the minus sign on Dx, and Option D satisfies x + z = 6 but fails the other two equations.

questions.question: Solve using determinants (Cramer's rule): 3x1 + x2 + 2x3 = 3; 2x1 - 3x2 - x3 = -3; x1 + 2x2 + x3 = 4.
questions.explanation: D = 3(-3 + 2) - 1(2 + 1) + 2(4 + 3) = -3 - 3 + 14 = 8, and replacing columns by (3, -3, 4) gives D1 = 8, D2 = 16 and D3 = -8. So x1 = 8/8 = 1, x2 = 16/8 = 2 and x3 = -8/8 = -1; check: 3(1) + 2 + 2(-1) = 3 and 1 + 2(2) + (-1) = 4. Option B has the wrong sign on x3, which happens if D3 is taken as +8, and Option C reverses every sign.

questions.question: Solve using determinants (Cramer's rule): x + 2y + 3z = 14; 2x + 3y + 4z = 20; 3x + 4y + 6z = 33.
questions.explanation: D = 1(18 - 16) - 2(12 - 12) + 3(8 - 9) = 2 - 0 - 3 = -1, and replacing columns by (14, 20, 33) gives Dx = -5, Dy = 6 and Dz = -7. Dividing by D = -1 gives x = 5, y = -6, z = 7; check: 5 + 2(-6) + 3(7) = 14. Option B forgets that D is negative and keeps the signs of Dx, Dy and Dz, and Option C swaps x and z.

questions.question: Solve using determinants (Cramer's rule): x - 2y + 3z = 11; 2x + y + 2z = 10; 3x + 2y + z = 9.
questions.explanation: D = 1(1 - 4) - (-2)(2 - 6) + 3(4 - 3) = -3 - 8 + 3 = -8, with Dx = -16, Dy = 0 and Dz = -24 when the columns are replaced by (11, 10, 9). So x = -16/-8 = 2, y = 0 and z = -24/-8 = 3; check: 2 - 0 + 3(3) = 11 and 3(2) + 0 + 3 = 9. Option A ignores the negative sign of D, and Option D swaps x and z.

questions.question: If A = [[1,-2,3],[5,1,-4]] and B = [[2,3,5],[1,4,-2]], find A - B.
questions.explanation: Subtract element by element: A - B = [[1 - 2, -2 - 3, 3 - 5],[5 - 1, 1 - 4, -4 - (-2)]] = [[-1,-5,-2],[4,-3,-2]]. Option C is B - A, with every sign reversed, and Option B is A + B. Option D slips on the last entry: -4 - (-2) = -4 + 2 = -2, not -6.

questions.question: For any square matrix A, the matrix A + A^T is always:
questions.explanation: Since (A + A^T)^T = A^T + (A^T)^T = A^T + A, the matrix A + A^T equals its own transpose, which is exactly the definition of a symmetric matrix. For example, A = [[1,2],[3,4]] gives A + A^T = [[2,5],[5,8]]. Option C describes A - A^T, which is the skew-symmetric one, and the example is neither the identity nor singular (its determinant is 16 - 25 = -9), so Option D and Option B fail.

questions.question: If A = [[1,2,3],[2,5,7],[3,7,3]] and B = [[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,1]], which statement is true?

options.b: AB is not equal to BA, because matrix multiplication is never commutative
options.d: AB = A, but BA is not defined

questions.explanation: B is the 3x3 identity matrix, and multiplying a square matrix by the identity on either side leaves it unchanged, so AB = BA = A. For instance, the first row of AB is (1(1) + 2(0) + 3(0), 1(0) + 2(1) + 3(0), 1(0) + 2(0) + 3(1)) = (1, 2, 3), the first row of A. Option B overgeneralises: matrix multiplication is not commutative in general, but the identity matrix commutes with every square matrix of its order.

questions.question: Let A = [[1,2,3],[2,5,7],[3,7,3]] and B = [[3,4,9],[6,5,1],[9,7,3]]. Find the product AB.
questions.explanation: Each entry of AB is a row of A times a column of B; for example, the (1,1) entry is 1(3) + 2(6) + 3(9) = 3 + 12 + 27 = 42 and the (2,1) entry is 2(3) + 5(6) + 7(9) = 99, giving AB = [[42,35,20],[99,82,44],[78,68,43]]. Option C is BA, whose (1,1) entry is 3(1) + 4(2) + 9(3) = 38, which shows AB is not equal to BA. Option D just multiplies matching elements, and Option A is the transpose of AB.

questions.question: If A = [[1,0,3],[2,1,5]], B = [[3,2,1],[1,1,1],[2,1,0]] and C = [[2,3],[1,2],[2,4]], find the product ABC (note that (AB)C = A(BC)).
questions.explanation: First AB = [[9,5,1],[17,10,3]], then (AB)C = [[9(2) + 5(1) + 1(2), 9(3) + 5(2) + 1(4)],[17(2) + 10(1) + 3(2), 17(3) + 10(2) + 3(4)]] = [[25,41],[50,83]]. Working the other way, BC = [[10,17],[5,9],[5,8]] and A(BC) gives the same [[25,41],[50,83]], confirming that matrix multiplication is associative. Option C leaves B out (it is just AC), Option A is the transpose of the correct result, and Option D uses the transpose of B by mistake.

questions.question: Find the inverse of the matrix A = [[2,-1],[1,1]].
questions.explanation: For [[a,b],[c,d]], A^-1 = (1/(ad - bc))[[d,-b],[-c,a]]. Here ad - bc = 2(1) - (-1)(1) = 3, so A^-1 = (1/3)[[1,1],[-1,2]]; check: A times this gives (1/3)[[3,0],[0,3]] = I. Option A swaps the diagonal entries but forgets to change the signs of b and c, Option C changes the signs but does not swap a and d, and Option B uses 2 - 1 = 1 as the determinant.

questions.question: Find the inverse of the matrix A = [[1,2,3],[1,3,5],[1,5,12]].
questions.explanation: |A| = 1(36 - 25) - 2(12 - 5) + 3(5 - 3) = 11 - 14 + 6 = 3. The cofactor matrix is [[11,-7,2],[-9,9,-3],[1,-2,1]], so adj A (its transpose) is [[11,-9,1],[-7,9,-2],[2,-3,1]] and A^-1 = adj A/3. Option C forgets to transpose the cofactor matrix, Option A has every sign reversed, and Option B uses the minors without the + - + cofactor signs.

questions.question: Find the inverse of the matrix A = [[1,2,3],[2,3,2],[3,3,4]].
questions.explanation: |A| = 1(12 - 6) - 2(8 - 6) + 3(6 - 9) = 6 - 4 - 9 = -7, and adj A = [[6,1,-5],[-2,-5,4],[-3,3,-1]]. Dividing by -7 gives A^-1 = (1/7)[[-6,-1,5],[2,5,-4],[3,-3,1]]. Option A divides by +7 instead of -7, Option D is the transpose of the correct inverse (the cofactor matrix was not transposed), and Option B leaves out the factor 1/7.

questions.question: Find the inverse of the matrix A = [[2,-1,3],[4,0,-1],[3,3,2]] (for example, by row canonical form).
questions.explanation: |A| = 2(0 + 3) - (-1)(8 + 3) + 3(12 - 0) = 6 + 11 + 36 = 53, and row-reducing [A | I] (or using adj A/|A|) gives A^-1 = (1/53)[[3,11,1],[-11,-5,14],[12,-9,4]]. Check the first entry of A x A^-1: 2(3) - 1(-11) + 3(12) = 53, divided by 53 gives 1. Option B is the transpose of the inverse, Option A has all signs reversed as if |A| were -53, and Option C uses minors without the cofactor signs.

questions.question: If A = [[-2,2,-3],[2,1,-6],[-1,-2,0]] and I is the 3x3 identity matrix, then A^3 + A^2 - 21A equals:
questions.explanation: Squaring gives A^2 = [[11,4,-6],[4,17,-12],[-2,-4,15]] and A^3 = A^2 x A = [[-8,38,-57],[38,49,-114],[-19,-38,30]]. The (1,1) entry of A^3 + A^2 - 21A is -8 + 11 - 21(-2) = 45, the other diagonal entries are 49 + 17 - 21 = 45 and 30 + 15 - 0 = 45, and every off-diagonal entry is 0 (e.g. 38 + 4 - 21(2) = 0), so the result is 45I. Option C reverses the digits of 45, and options A and B do not match the diagonal value of 45 that the working produces.

questions.question: If A = [[3,6],[2,1]], find A^-1 (inverting the result again gives back A, since (A^-1)^-1 = A).
questions.explanation: |A| = 3(1) - 6(2) = -9, so A^-1 = (1/-9)[[1,-6],[-2,3]] = (1/9)[[-1,6],[2,-3]]. Inverting this again gives back [[3,6],[2,1]], which illustrates (A^-1)^-1 = A. Option C uses +9 as the determinant, Option B uses 3 + 12 = 15, and Option D is the transpose of the correct inverse.

questions.question: Solve the following system with the help of matrices: 5x - 6y + 4z = 15; 7x + 4y - 3z = 19; 2x + y + 6z = 46.
questions.explanation: D = 5(24 + 3) - (-6)(42 + 6) + 4(7 - 8) = 135 + 288 - 4 = 419, and replacing columns by (15, 19, 46) gives Dx = 1257, Dy = 1676 and Dz = 2514, so x = 3, y = 4 and z = 6 (X = A^-1 B gives the same). Check: 5(3) - 6(4) + 4(6) = 15 and 2(3) + 4 + 6(6) = 46. Option A swaps x and y, which fails the first equation (20 - 18 + 24 = 26).

questions.question: To solve x + 2y + 3z = 14; 2x + 3y + 4z = 20; 3x + 4y + 6z = 33 by the matrix method X = A^-1 B, the inverse of the coefficient matrix A = [[1,2,3],[2,3,4],[3,4,6]] is needed. A^-1 is:
questions.explanation: |A| = 1(18 - 16) - 2(12 - 12) + 3(8 - 9) = 2 - 0 - 3 = -1 and adj A = [[2,0,-1],[0,-3,2],[-1,2,-1]], so A^-1 = adj A/(-1) = [[-2,0,1],[0,3,-2],[1,-2,1]]. Then X = A^-1 B = (-28 + 0 + 33, 0 + 60 - 66, 14 - 40 + 33) = (5, -6, 7). Option D is adj A itself, forgetting to divide by |A| = -1, while Option A and Option B use minors without the + - + cofactor signs.

questions.question: Solve the following system with the help of matrices: 2x + 3y - z = 1; 3x + 5y + 2z = 8; x - 2y - 3z = -1.
questions.explanation: |A| = 2(-15 + 4) - 3(-9 - 2) + (-1)(-6 - 5) = -22 + 33 + 11 = 22, and X = A^-1 B (or Cramer's rule with Dx = 66, Dy = -22, Dz = 44) gives x = 3, y = -1, z = 2. Check: 2(3) + 3(-1) - 2 = 1 and 3 - 2(-1) - 3(2) = -1. Option D drops the negative sign on y, which fails the first equation (6 + 3 - 2 = 7), and Option C reverses every sign.

questions.question: Solve by elementary row transformations (row equivalent canonical matrix): 2x - y + z = 1; x + 4y - 3z = -2; 3x + 2y - z = 0.
questions.explanation: Swap R1 and R2, then R2 - 2R1 gives (0, -9, 7 | 5) and R3 - 3R1 gives (0, -10, 8 | 6); next 9R3 - 10R2 gives (0, 0, 2 | 4), so z = 2. Back-substituting, -9y + 7(2) = 5 gives y = 1, and x + 4(1) - 3(2) = -2 gives x = 0. Option A swaps y and z and fails the first equation (0 - 2 + 1 = -1), and Option C has the signs of y and z reversed.

questions.question: Solve by elementary row transformations: 2x + 3y - 2z = 5; x - 2y + 3z = 2; 4x - y + 4z = 1. Which statement is correct?

options.a: The system has infinitely many solutions
options.b: The system has the unique solution (1, 1, 0)
options.c: The system has no solution (it is inconsistent)
options.d: The system has the unique solution (0, 1, -1)

questions.explanation: Here |A| = 0, so check consistency: the first equation plus 2 times the second gives 4x - y + 4z = 5 + 2(2) = 9, but the third equation says 4x - y + 4z = 1. The equations contradict each other (rank of A = 2 but rank of [A | B] = 3), so there is no solution. Option A is the tempting mistake of assuming |A| = 0 always means infinitely many solutions, while Option B and Option D satisfy only the first equation.

questions.question: A manufacturer produces three products P, Q and R, which he sells in two markets. Annual sales volumes are given by the matrix [[4000,3000,2000],[3000,2000,1000]] (rows = Markets 1, 2; columns = Products P, Q, R). The unit sale prices of P, Q and R are N2.50, N2.00 and N1.50 respectively, and their unit costs are N2.00, N1.50 and N1.00. Using matrix multiplication, find the total revenue from both markets.
questions.explanation: Revenue = sales matrix x price vector: Market 1 = 4,000(2.50) + 3,000(2.00) + 2,000(1.50) = 10,000 + 6,000 + 3,000 = N19,000 and Market 2 = 3,000(2.50) + 2,000(2.00) + 1,000(1.50) = 7,500 + 4,000 + 1,500 = N13,000. Total revenue is 19,000 + 13,000 = N32,000. Option B uses the unit costs and gives total cost, Option D is Market 1 only, and Option C is the gross profit.

questions.question: A manufacturer produces three products P, Q and R, which he sells in two markets. Annual sales volumes are given by the matrix [[4000,3000,2000],[3000,2000,1000]] (rows = Markets 1, 2; columns = Products P, Q, R). The unit sale prices of P, Q and R are N2.50, N2.00 and N1.50 respectively, and their unit costs are N2.00, N1.50 and N1.00. Using matrix multiplication, find the total gross profit from both markets.
questions.explanation: Profit per unit is 2.50 - 2.00 = 0.50, 2.00 - 1.50 = 0.50 and 1.50 - 1.00 = 0.50, so Market 1 profit = 0.50(4,000 + 3,000 + 2,000) = N4,500 and Market 2 profit = 0.50(3,000 + 2,000 + 1,000) = N3,000, a total of N7,500. Equivalently, revenue N32,000 minus cost N24,500 = N7,500. Option A is the total cost, Option C counts only Market 1, and Option B adds the cost to the revenue instead of subtracting it.

questions.question: A television manufacturer produces three types of TV, A, B and C, which he sells in two markets. Annual sales volumes are given by the matrix [[10000,2000,18000],[6000,20000,8000]] (rows = Markets 1, 2; columns = types A, B, C). The unit sale prices of A, B and C are N1,500, N3,000 and N4,000 respectively, and their unit costs are N1,000, N2,000 and N3,000. Using matrix multiplication, find the total revenue from both markets.

A television manufacturer produces three types of TV, A, B and C, which he sells in two markets. Annual sales volumes are given by the matrix [[10000,2000,18000],[6000,20000,8000]] (rows = Markets 1, 2; columns = types A, B, C). The unit sale prices of A, B and C are N1,500, N3,000 and N4,000 respectively, and their unit costs are N1,000, N2,000 and N3,000. Using matrix multiplication, find the total gross profit from both markets.
questions.explanation: Profit per unit is (500, 1,000, 1,000), so Market 1 profit = 10,000(500) + 2,000(1,000) + 18,000(1,000) = 5,000,000 + 2,000,000 + 18,000,000 = N25,000,000 and Market 2 profit = 6,000(500) + 20,000(1,000) + 8,000(1,000) = 3,000,000 + 20,000,000 + 8,000,000 = N31,000,000. The total is N56,000,000, which is revenue N194,000,000 minus cost N138,000,000. Option B is the total cost, Option D is Market 1 only, and Option C adds cost to revenue instead of subtracting.

questions.question: The daily cost of operating a hospital (C) is a linear function of the number of inpatients (I) and outpatients (O) plus a fixed cost (x), i.e. C = x + yO + zI. Over three days: Day 1, cost N7,000 with 50 inpatients and 10 outpatients; Day 2, N6,500 with 40 inpatients and 10 outpatients; Day 3, N7,500 with 50 inpatients and 15 outpatients. Setting up the linear system and solving it with the matrix inverse, find x, y and z.
questions.explanation: Each day gives an equation C = x + yO + zI: x + 10y + 50z = 7,000, x + 10y + 40z = 6,500 and x + 15y + 50z = 7,500. Subtracting the second from the first gives 10z = 500, so z = 50; subtracting the first from the third gives 5y = 500, so y = 100; then x = 7,000 - 1,000 - 2,500 = 3,500 (the matrix inverse method gives the same values). Option D swaps y and z by attaching the outpatient figures to z, while Option A and Option C fit Days 1 and 3 but fail Day 2, giving N6,600 and N6,300 instead of N6,500.

questions.question: A special food for athletes is to be made from two foods, Food X and Food Y, so that it contains exactly 16 ounces of vitamin A, 44 ounces of vitamin B and 12 ounces of vitamin C. Each pound of Food X contains 1 ounce of A, 5 ounces of B and 1 ounce of C; each pound of Food Y contains 2 ounces of A, 1 ounce of B and 1 ounce of C. How many pounds of each food should be used?

options.a: 4 pounds of Food X and 8 pounds of Food Y
options.b: 10 pounds of Food X and 3 pounds of Food Y
options.c: 6 pounds of Food X and 5 pounds of Food Y
options.d: 8 pounds of Food X and 4 pounds of Food Y

questions.explanation: Let X and Y be the pounds of each food: vitamin A gives X + 2Y = 16, vitamin B gives 5X + Y = 44 and vitamin C gives X + Y = 12. Subtracting the C equation from the A equation gives Y = 4, so X = 8, and 5(8) + 4 = 44 confirms vitamin B. Option A swaps the foods (4 + 2(8) = 20, not 16), while Option C and Option B meet the vitamin A requirement but not B or C.

questions.question: Solve the following system by Cramer's rule: x + 2y + z = 0; x - 2y - 2z = 0; 3x + y + 2z = 11.
questions.explanation: The coefficient determinant is D = 1(-4 + 2) - 2(2 + 6) + 1(1 + 6) = -11, and replacing each column in turn by (0, 0, 11) gives Dx = -22, Dy = 33 and Dz = -44. So x = -22/-11 = 2, y = 33/-11 = -3 and z = -44/-11 = 4, which check in all three equations (for example 6 - 3 + 8 = 11). Option C forgets that D is negative, option B drops the sign of y, and option A swaps the values of x and z.

questions.question: The system 3x + 2y - 5z = -8; 2x + 3y + 6z = 37; x - y + 6z = 7 is to be solved by Cramer's rule. What is the value of the coefficient determinant D?
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row, D = 3[(3)(6) - (6)(-1)] - 2[(2)(6) - (6)(1)] + (-5)[(2)(-1) - (3)(1)] = 3(24) - 2(6) - 5(-5) = 72 - 12 + 25 = 85. Option C forgets the minus sign on the second cofactor term (72 + 12 + 25), option B treats (-5)(-5) as -25 (72 - 12 - 25), and option A is a sign slip on the whole determinant.

questions.question: Solve by Cramer's rule: 2x + y + 2z = 10; x - y + 2z = 5; x + y + z = 6.
questions.explanation: The coefficient determinant is D = 2(-1 - 2) - 1(1 - 2) + 2(1 + 1) = -6 + 1 + 4 = -1, and replacing columns by (10, 5, 6) gives Dx = -1, Dy = -2 and Dz = -3. Hence x = -1/-1 = 1, y = -2/-1 = 2 and z = -3/-1 = 3, which check: 2 + 2 + 6 = 10, 1 - 2 + 6 = 5 and 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. Option D ignores the negative sign of D, while options C and A put the right numbers in the wrong order.

questions.question: Solve by Cramer's rule, where a and b are non-zero constants: x/a + y/b = 2; ax - by = a^2 - b^2.
questions.explanation: Here D = (1/a)(-b) - (1/b)(a) = -(a^2 + b^2)/(ab), Dx = 2(-b) - (1/b)(a^2 - b^2) = -(a^2 + b^2)/b and Dy = (1/a)(a^2 - b^2) - 2a = -(a^2 + b^2)/a. So x = Dx/D = a and y = Dy/D = b, and indeed a/a + b/b = 2 and a(a) - b(b) = a^2 - b^2. Option C swaps a and b and fails the first equation unless a = b, while options D and A have the wrong signs and fail the first equation.

questions.question: Solve the system: x + 2y - z = 2; 2x + y + z = 1; x + 5y - 4z = 5.

options.a: It has the unique solution x = -1, y = 2, z = 1
options.c: It has the unique solution x = 1, y = 1, z = 1
options.d: It has infinitely many solutions, for example x = -1, y = 2, z = 1

questions.explanation: The third equation adds nothing new: 3(x + 2y - z) - (2x + y + z) = x + 5y - 4z and 3(2) - 1 = 5, so there are only two independent equations in three unknowns. Solving the first two gives x = -z and y = z + 1 for any value of z, so there are infinitely many solutions, and z = 1 gives (-1, 2, 1). Option A is tempting because (-1, 2, 1) does satisfy all three equations, but it is not the only solution, and option B is wrong because the equations are consistent.

questions.question: Solve the system: x + 2y - 3z = -1; 5x + 3y - 4z = 2; 3x - y + 2z = 7.

options.a: It has the unique solution x = 1, y = -1, z = 0
options.b: It has the unique solution x = 1, y = 1, z = 1

questions.explanation: The left side of the third equation equals the second minus twice the first: (5x + 3y - 4z) - 2(x + 2y - 3z) = 3x - y + 2z. The same combination of right sides gives 2 - 2(-1) = 4, so the first two equations force 3x - y + 2z = 4, which contradicts 3x - y + 2z = 7; the system is inconsistent and has no solution. Option A satisfies the first two equations but gives 3 + 1 + 0 = 4, not 7, in the third, and option C would need the right sides to follow the same combination (7 would have to be 4).

questions.question: Solve the system: x + 2y - 3z = 4; x + 3y + z = 11; 2x + 5y - 4z = 13; 2x + 6y + 2z = 22.

options.b: It has no solution, because there are four equations but only three unknowns

questions.explanation: The fourth equation is just twice the second, so it repeats the same condition. Subtracting the first equation from the second gives y + 4z = 7, and subtracting twice the first from the third gives y + 2z = 5, so 2z = 2, z = 1, y = 3 and x = 4 - 6 + 3 = 1; (1, 3, 1) satisfies all four equations (for example 2 + 18 + 2 = 22). Option B is wrong because extra equations do not rule out a solution when they are consistent, and option D fails the first equation (3 + 2 - 3 = 2, not 4).

questions.question: Solve the system: x + y + z = 4; 2x - y + z = 3; x - 2y + 3z = 5.
questions.explanation: Adding the first two equations eliminates y and gives 3x + 2z = 7, while doubling the first and adding the third gives 3x + 5z = 13. Subtracting, 3z = 6, so z = 2, then x = (7 - 4)/3 = 1 and y = 4 - 1 - 2 = 1. Options C and A satisfy x + y + z = 4 but fail the second equation (4 - 1 + 1 = 4 and 2 - 2 + 1 = 1, not 3), and option B has every sign reversed.

questions.question: Solve the simultaneous equations 2x - 3y = 3 and 4x - y = 11 using determinants.
questions.explanation: The coefficient determinant is D = (2)(-1) - (-3)(4) = -2 + 12 = 10, Dx = (3)(-1) - (-3)(11) = 30 and Dy = (2)(11) - (3)(4) = 10, so x = 30/10 = 3 and y = 10/10 = 1. Check: 6 - 3 = 3 and 12 - 1 = 11. Option C divides D by Dx instead of Dx by D, option D swaps x and y, and option B has a sign slip in y (6 + 3 is not 3).

questions.question: Find the values of x, y, z and a which satisfy the matrix equation [[x + 3, 2y + x],[z - 1, 4a - 6]] = [[0, -7],[3, 2a]].
questions.explanation: Two matrices are equal only when their corresponding entries are equal, so x + 3 = 0, 2y + x = -7, z - 1 = 3 and 4a - 6 = 2a. These give x = -3, then 2y - 3 = -7 so y = -2, z = 4, and 2a = 6 so a = 3. Option A makes a sign slip in x + 3 = 0, option B subtracts 1 instead of adding it when solving z - 1 = 3, and option D adds 2a to the left side instead of subtracting it, giving 6a = 6.

questions.question: If A = [[1, 2],[-1, 3]] and B = [[2, 1],[1, 1]], find AB and BA.
questions.explanation: Multiply rows of the first matrix by columns of the second: AB = [[1(2) + 2(1), 1(1) + 2(1)],[-1(2) + 3(1), -1(1) + 3(1)]] = [[4, 3],[1, 2]], while BA = [[2(1) + 1(-1), 2(2) + 1(3)],[1(1) + 1(-1), 1(2) + 1(3)]] = [[1, 7],[0, 5]]. Since AB != BA, matrix multiplication is not commutative, so option C is wrong. Option B swaps the two products, and option D multiplies matching entries instead of rows by columns.

questions.question: If A = [[3, 1, 2],[1, 0, 1]] and B = [[1, -1],[2, 1],[3, 1]], find AB.
questions.explanation: A is 2 x 3 and B is 3 x 2, so AB is defined and is 2 x 2. Row 1 of A times the columns of B gives 3 + 2 + 6 = 11 and -3 + 1 + 2 = 0, and row 2 gives 1 + 0 + 3 = 4 and -1 + 0 + 1 = 0, so AB = [[11, 0],[4, 0]]. Option A is BA, the product in the reverse order, option C drops the minus sign in 3(-1), and option D is wrong because the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B.

questions.question: A matrix is written as A = [a_ij], where i = 1, 2, 3 and j = 1, 2, 3, 4 (the first subscript i gives the row and the second subscript j gives the column). Which of the following writes A correctly in tabular form?
questions.explanation: Since i runs from 1 to 3 and j from 1 to 4, A has 3 rows and 4 columns (order 3 x 4), and the entry a_ij sits in row i, column j, so row 1 is a11, a12, a13, a14 and so on. Option A places a_ij in row j and column i, giving a 4 x 3 arrangement. Option B leaves out the fourth column, and option D uses 4 rows and 3 columns, swapping the ranges of i and j.

questions.question: Write as a single matrix: 2[[6, 1],[0, -3],[-1, 2]] - 3[[4, 2],[0, 1],[-5, -1]].
questions.explanation: First multiply each matrix by its scalar: 2[[6, 1],[0, -3],[-1, 2]] = [[12, 2],[0, -6],[-2, 4]] and 3[[4, 2],[0, 1],[-5, -1]] = [[12, 6],[0, 3],[-15, -3]]. Subtracting entry by entry gives [[0, -4],[0, -9],[-2 + 15, 4 + 3]] = [[0, -4],[0, -9],[13, 7]]. Option B adds the two matrices instead of subtracting, option C slips on -2 - (-15), and option D cannot be right because combining two 3 x 2 matrices must give a 3 x 2 matrix, not a 2 x 3 one.

questions.question: Solve the matrix equation 3X + [[1, 0, 2],[2, 1, 3],[4, -1, 5]] = [[-2, 3, 1],[-1, -2, 0],[0, 1, 5]].
questions.explanation: Subtract the known matrix from both sides to get 3X = [[-2 - 1, 3 - 0, 1 - 2],[-1 - 2, -2 - 1, 0 - 3],[0 - 4, 1 + 1, 5 - 5]] = [[-3, 3, -1],[-3, -3, -3],[-4, 2, 0]], then divide every entry by 3 to get X = [[-1, 1, -1/3],[-1, -1, -1],[-4/3, 2/3, 0]]. Option A stops at 3X and forgets to divide by 3. Option B adds the matrices instead of subtracting, and option D slips on the sign of 0 - 4.

questions.question: Solve the matrix equation X + 2I = [[3, -1],[1, 2]], where I is the 2 x 2 identity matrix.
questions.explanation: Here 2I = [[2, 0],[0, 2]], so X = [[3, -1],[1, 2]] - [[2, 0],[0, 2]] = [[1, -1],[1, 0]]. Option B subtracts 2 from every entry, forgetting that the identity matrix has zeros off the main diagonal. Option C adds 2I instead of subtracting it, and option D subtracts I instead of 2I.

questions.question: Write as a single matrix: [[2, -2, -1],[1, 1, -2],[1, 0, -1]] [[-1, -2, 5],[-1, -1, 3],[-1, -2, 4]].
questions.explanation: Multiply rows by columns: for example, the (1, 1) entry is 2(-1) + (-2)(-1) + (-1)(-1) = -2 + 2 + 1 = 1 and the (1, 2) entry is 2(-2) + (-2)(-1) + (-1)(-2) = -4 + 2 + 2 = 0; working through all nine entries gives the identity matrix I, so the two matrices are inverses of each other. Option A multiplies matching entries instead of rows by columns. Options B and D do not fit the row-by-column sums, since every diagonal entry comes out as +1 and every off-diagonal entry as 0.

questions.question: Write as a single matrix: [[3, 1, -1],[0, -1, 2]] [[1, -1],[0, 2],[1, 0]].
questions.explanation: The first matrix is 2 x 3 and the second is 3 x 2, so the product is 2 x 2. Row 1 gives 3(1) + 1(0) + (-1)(1) = 2 and 3(-1) + 1(2) + (-1)(0) = -1, and row 2 gives 0 + 0 + 2(1) = 2 and 0 + (-1)(2) + 0 = -2, so the answer is [[2, -1],[2, -2]]. Option A multiplies in the reverse order, option B treats (-1)(1) as +1, and option D is wrong because the number of columns of the first matrix (3) matches the number of rows of the second (3).

questions.question: If A = [[1, 4],[2, 1]], B = [[-3, 2],[4, 0]] and C = [[1, 0],[0, 2]], find A^2 + BC.
questions.explanation: A^2 = AA = [[1 + 8, 4 + 4],[2 + 2, 8 + 1]] = [[9, 8],[4, 9]] and BC = [[-3 + 0, 0 + 4],[4 + 0, 0 + 0]] = [[-3, 4],[4, 0]], so A^2 + BC = [[6, 12],[8, 9]]. Option A uses CB instead of BC, which is different because matrix multiplication is not commutative. Option B squares each entry of A instead of multiplying A by itself, and option D multiplies B and C entry by entry.

questions.question: If A = [[3, 1],[-2, 3]], find |A|.
questions.explanation: For a 2 x 2 matrix [[a, b],[c, d]], |A| = ad - bc, so |A| = 3(3) - (1)(-2) = 9 + 2 = 11. Option A forgets that subtracting -2 means adding 2 (9 - 2 = 7), and option B subtracts the main-diagonal product from the other one, (1)(-2) - 3(3) = -11. Option D makes both of these mistakes at once.

questions.question: If A = [[3, 2, 1],[0, 1, -2],[1, 3, 4]], find det A by cofactor expansion (about the first row or the first column).
questions.explanation: Expanding about the first row with signs +, -, +: |A| = 3|1 -2; 3 4| - 2|0 -2; 1 4| + 1|0 1; 1 3| = 3(4 + 6) - 2(0 + 2) + 1(0 - 1) = 30 - 4 - 1 = 25, and expanding about the first column gives the same value, 3(10) - 0 + 1(-4 - 1) = 25. Option B forgets the minus sign on the middle term (30 + 4 + 1), option C takes the last minor as +1 instead of -1, and option D leaves out the middle term altogether.

questions.question: Use Cramer's rule to solve the system: -4x + 2y - 9z = 2; 3x + 4y + z = 5; x - 3y + 2z = 8.
questions.explanation: The coefficient determinant is |A| = -4(8 + 3) - 2(6 - 1) - 9(-9 - 4) = -44 - 10 + 117 = 63, and replacing each column in turn by the constants 2, 5, 8 gives |A_x| = 441, |A_y| = -189 and |A_z| = -252. So x = 441/63 = 7, y = -189/63 = -3 and z = -252/63 = -4 (check: -4(7) + 2(-3) - 9(-4) = -28 - 6 + 36 = 2). Option A comes from a sign slip that makes |A| = -63, option C divides |A| by each determinant the wrong way round, and option D forgets to divide by |A|.

questions.question: Expand the determinant |1 2 0; 3 -1 4; -2 1 3|.
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row: 1|-1 4; 1 3| - 2|3 4; -2 3| + 0 = 1(-3 - 4) - 2(9 + 8) = -7 - 34 = -41. Option A forgets the minus sign on the second term (-7 + 34 = 27), and option D works out the second minor as 9 - 8 instead of 9 - (-8). Option B has the right size but the wrong sign.

questions.question: Find the values of x if |3 1 x; -1 3 4; x 1 0| = -30.
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row: 3(0 - 4) - 1(0 - 4x) + x(-1 - 3x) = -12 + 4x - x - 3x^2 = -3x^2 + 3x - 12. Setting this equal to -30 gives 3x^2 - 3x - 18 = 0, i.e. x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2) = 0, so x = 3 or x = -2. Option A reverses the signs of both roots, a factorising slip, and options B and C do not satisfy the equation (for example, x = 4 makes the determinant -48, not -30).

questions.question: Find the values of x if |1 2 1; 2 x 2; 3 6 x| = 0.
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row: 1(x^2 - 12) - 2(2x - 6) + 1(12 - 3x) = x^2 - 12 - 4x + 12 + 12 - 3x = x^2 - 7x + 12. Setting this to zero gives (x - 3)(x - 4) = 0, so x = 3 or x = 4. Option B forgets the minus sign on the middle term, giving x^2 + x - 12 = 0, option C gets the sign of the last term wrong, giving x^2 - x - 12 = 0, and option A reverses the signs of both roots.

questions.question: Use Cramer's rule to solve the system 2x + 2y + z = 1; x - y + 6z = 21; 3x + 2y - z = -4. The solution (x, y, z) is
questions.explanation: By Cramer's rule, D = |2 2 1; 1 -1 6; 3 2 -1| = 2(1 - 12) - 2(-1 - 18) + 1(2 + 3) = -22 + 38 + 5 = 21, and replacing each column in turn by (1, 21, -4) gives Dx = 21, Dy = -42 and Dz = 63. So x = 21/21 = 1, y = -42/21 = -2 and z = 63/21 = 3, which checks in all three equations. Option D comes from losing the minus sign on Dy, option C swaps Dx and Dz, and option A divides by -21 instead of 21.

questions.question: Use Cramer's rule to solve the system 3x - 4y = -2 and x + y = 6. The solution (x, y) is
questions.explanation: Here D = |3 -4; 1 1| = 3(1) - (-4)(1) = 7, Dx = |-2 -4; 6 1| = -2 + 24 = 22 and Dy = |3 -2; 1 6| = 18 + 2 = 20. So x = Dx/D = 22/7 and y = Dy/D = 20/7; check: 22/7 + 20/7 = 42/7 = 6. Option A takes D as 3 - 4 = -1, forgetting that subtracting -4 adds 4, option B slips on Dx (-2 - 24 instead of -2 + 24), and option D swaps the two values.

questions.question: Find k if A = [[k - 2, 1],[5, k + 2]] is singular.
questions.explanation: A singular matrix has determinant zero, so (k - 2)(k + 2) - (1)(5) = 0, giving k^2 - 4 - 5 = 0, k^2 = 9 and k = 3 or k = -3. Option C forgets to subtract the product 1 x 5, and option B stops at k^2 = 9 without taking the square root.

questions.question: Find the adjoint of A = [[1, 0, -1],[1, 3, 1],[0, 1, 2]].
questions.explanation: The adjoint is the transpose of the matrix of cofactors. The cofactors are C11 = 5, C12 = -2, C13 = 1, C21 = -1, C22 = 2, C23 = -1, C31 = 3, C32 = -2 and C33 = 3, so transposing the cofactor matrix [[5, -2, 1],[-1, 2, -1],[3, -2, 3]] gives adj A = [[5, -1, 3],[-2, 2, -2],[1, -1, 3]]. Option B is the cofactor matrix before transposing, option A ignores the (-1)^(i+j) signs, and option D is A^-1 (adj A divided by |A| = 4), not the adjoint.

questions.question: Find the inverse of A = [[3, 4],[1, 2]].
questions.explanation: For a 2 x 2 matrix [[a, b],[c, d]], swap a and d, change the signs of b and c, and divide by the determinant. Here |A| = 3(2) - 4(1) = 2 and adj A = [[2, -4],[-1, 3]], so A^-1 = (1/2)[[2, -4],[-1, 3]] = [[1, -2],[-1/2, 3/2]]. Option C swaps the diagonal but forgets the sign changes, option B changes the signs without swapping, and option A wrongly uses 6 + 4 = 10 as the determinant.

questions.question: Let A = [[1, -3],[-2, 7]]. Which matrix B satisfies AB = BA = I, so that B = A^-1?
questions.explanation: Since |A| = 1(7) - (-3)(-2) = 7 - 6 = 1, A^-1 is just adj A = [[7, 3],[2, 1]] (swap 1 and 7, change the signs of -3 and -2). Check: AB = [[7 - 6, 3 - 3],[-14 + 14, -6 + 7]] = [[1, 0],[0, 1]] = I, and BA gives I as well. Option C swaps the diagonal but keeps the original signs of -3 and -2, and option A uses |A| = -1 instead of 1.

questions.question: Find the inverse, if it exists, of the matrix A = [[0, -2, -3],[1, 3, 3],[-1, -2, -2]].

options.b: The inverse does not exist because |A| = 0

questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row, |A| = 0(-6 + 6) - (-2)(-2 + 3) + (-3)(-2 + 3) = 0 + 2 - 3 = -1, so the inverse exists. The cofactors give adj A = [[0, 2, 3],[-1, -3, -3],[1, 2, 2]], and dividing by |A| = -1 gives A^-1 = [[0, -2, -3],[1, 3, 3],[-1, -2, -2]], which is A itself (so A x A = I). Option D is adj A without dividing by -1, and option C forgets to transpose the cofactor matrix.

questions.question: Use matrices to find the solution set of x + y - 2z = 3; 3x - y + z = 5; 3x + 3y - 6z = 9. Which statement is correct?

options.a: |A| = 0 and the equations are inconsistent, so the system has no solution
options.b: |A| = -42, so the system has a unique solution
options.c: |A| = 0 and the third equation is 3 times the first, so the system has infinitely many solutions
options.d: |A| = 0, so the only solution is x = y = z = 0

questions.explanation: The coefficient determinant is |A| = 1(6 - 3) - 1(-18 - 3) + (-2)(9 + 3) = 3 + 21 - 24 = 0, so A has no inverse and there is no unique solution. The third equation is exactly 3 times the first (3x + 3y - 6z = 9), so only two independent equations remain and the system has infinitely many solutions, for example (2, 1, 0) and (9/4, 11/4, 1). Option A would be right only if the equations contradicted each other, for example if the third right-hand side were 8 instead of 9, and option B comes from a sign slip on the middle term of the expansion.

questions.question: Use matrices to find the solution set of 4x + 8y + z = -6; 2x - 3y + 2z = 0; x + 7y - 3z = -8.
Which of the following matrices is non-singular?
questions.explanation: A matrix is non-singular when its determinant is not zero. For [[1, 2, 1],[3, 1, -2],[0, 1, -1]], the determinant is 1(-1 + 2) - 2(-3 - 0) + 1(3 - 0) = 1 + 6 + 3 = 10, which is non-zero. Option C gives 1(24 - 10) - 2(-18 + 20) - 1(-6 + 16) = 14 - 4 - 10 = 0, option D has its third row equal to 3 times its first row, and option B has its second row equal to 2 times its first row, so all three are singular.

questions.question: Which of the following matrices is skew-symmetric?
questions.explanation: A skew-symmetric matrix satisfies A^t = -A, so a_ij = -a_ji for every pair and every main-diagonal element must be 0. In [[0, 3, -5],[-3, 0, 6],[5, -6, 0]] the diagonal is all zeros and each mirror pair is opposite in sign (3 and -3, -5 and 5, 6 and -6). Option D has a zero diagonal but its pairs are equal, which makes it symmetric rather than skew-symmetric, and option B fails because its leading element is 1 instead of 0.

questions.question: Which of the following matrices is symmetric?
questions.explanation: A matrix is symmetric when A^t = A, that is a_ij = a_ji, so it looks the same when reflected across the main diagonal. In [[2, 6, 7],[6, -2, 3],[7, 3, 0]] the mirror pairs match: a12 = a21 = 6, a13 = a31 = 7 and a23 = a32 = 3. Option A is skew-symmetric because its pairs are opposite in sign, and option B has a12 = 6 but a21 = 7, so its transpose is different.

questions.question: Find K such that the matrix [[1, 2, -1],[-3, 4, K],[-4, 2, 6]] is singular.
questions.explanation: Set the determinant equal to zero: 1(4 x 6 - 2K) - 2((-3)(6) - (-4)K) + (-1)((-3)(2) - 4(-4)) = (24 - 2K) - 2(-18 + 4K) - (-6 + 16) = 50 - 10K. So 50 - 10K = 0 and K = 5. Option C comes from adding the middle term of the expansion instead of subtracting it (6K - 22 = 0), and option D is a sign slip when solving 50 - 10K = 0.

questions.question: Find k such that the matrix [[1, 1, -2],[3, -1, 1],[k, 3, -6]] is singular.
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row: 1((-1)(-6) - (1)(3)) - 1((3)(-6) - (1)(k)) + (-2)((3)(3) - (-1)(k)) = 3 - (-18 - k) - 2(9 + k) = 3 + 18 + k - 18 - 2k = 3 - k. Setting 3 - k = 0 gives k = 3. Option C comes from adding the middle term instead of subtracting it (-33 - 3k = 0), and option D writes the last minor as 9 - k instead of 9 + k.

questions.question: Find the inverse, if it exists, of A = [[1, 3],[2, -1]].
questions.explanation: |A| = 1(-1) - 3(2) = -1 - 6 = -7, which is non-zero, so the inverse exists. adj A = [[-1, -3],[-2, 1]], so A^-1 = (1/-7)[[-1, -3],[-2, 1]] = [[1/7, 3/7],[2/7, -1/7]]. Option C divides by +7 instead of -7, option A forgets to change the signs of 3 and 2, and option D wrongly computes the determinant as -1 + 6 = 5.

questions.question: Find the inverse, if it exists, of A = [[1, 2, 3],[-1, 0, 4],[0, 2, 2]].

options.a: The inverse does not exist because |A| = 0

questions.explanation: |A| = 1(0 - 8) - 2(-2 - 0) + 3(-2 - 0) = -8 + 4 - 6 = -10, so A is non-singular. The cofactors give adj A = [[-8, 2, 8],[2, 2, -7],[-2, -2, 2]], and A^-1 = adj A/(-10) = [[4/5, -1/5, -4/5],[-1/5, -1/5, 7/10],[1/5, 1/5, -1/5]]. Option D divides by +10 instead of -10, and option B forgets to transpose the cofactor matrix.

questions.question: Use matrices to find the solution set of x + y - 2z = 3; 3x - y + z = 0; 3x + 3y - 6z = 8.

options.b: Infinitely many solutions, because the third equation is a multiple of the first
options.d: No solution: |A| = 0 and the equations are inconsistent

questions.explanation: The coefficient matrix [[1, 1, -2],[3, -1, 1],[3, 3, -6]] has |A| = 1(6 - 3) - 1(-18 - 3) + (-2)(9 + 3) = 3 + 21 - 24 = 0, so there is no unique solution. Multiplying the first equation by 3 gives 3x + 3y - 6z = 9, but the third equation says 3x + 3y - 6z = 8, and 9 cannot equal 8, so the equations are inconsistent and the solution set is empty. Option B would only be true if the third right-hand side were 9, and options A and C ignore that |A| = 0 rules out a unique solution.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly defines row and column vectors?

options.a: A row vector is a matrix whose rows are all equal; a column vector is a matrix whose columns are all equal
options.b: A row vector is a square matrix written in one line; a column vector is its transpose of the same order
options.c: A row vector is a matrix with only one column (order m x 1); a column vector is a matrix with only one row (order 1 x n)
options.d: A row vector is a matrix with only one row (order 1 x n); a column vector is a matrix with only one column (order m x 1)

questions.explanation: A row vector (row matrix) has exactly one row, so its order is 1 x n, for example [2 5 7] is 1 x 3; a column vector (column matrix) has exactly one column, so its order is m x 1, for example [[3],[5],[8]] is 3 x 1. Option C swaps the two definitions, and option A confuses having one row with having rows that are equal.

questions.question: Which of the following defines an identity matrix?

options.a: Any square matrix whose determinant is 1
options.b: A matrix in which every element is 0
options.c: A matrix in which every element is 1
options.d: A square matrix with 1 in every position of the main diagonal and 0 everywhere else

questions.explanation: The identity (unit) matrix I has a_ij = 1 when i = j and a_ij = 0 when i != j, for example I = [[1, 0],[0, 1]], and it satisfies AI = IA = A. Option C is a matrix of ones, which does not leave A unchanged when multiplied, and option B is the null matrix. Option A fails because a matrix such as [[1, 1],[0, 1]] has determinant 1 but is not the identity.

questions.question: Which of the following defines a symmetric matrix?

options.a: A square matrix A for which A^2 = A
options.b: A square matrix A for which A^t = A, that is a_ij = a_ji for all i and j
options.c: A square matrix A for which A^t = -A
options.d: A square matrix A for which A^-1 = A

questions.explanation: A symmetric matrix equals its own transpose, so each element matches its mirror image across the main diagonal, as in [[1, 2, 3],[2, 5, 7],[3, 7, 3]]. Option C defines a skew-symmetric matrix, option D describes a matrix that is its own inverse, and option A describes an idempotent matrix.

questions.question: Which of the following defines a diagonal matrix?

options.a: A matrix in which all the elements are equal
options.b: A square matrix in which every element on the main diagonal is zero
options.c: A square matrix in which a_ij = -a_ji for all i and j
options.d: A square matrix in which every element off the main diagonal is zero (a_ij = 0 whenever i != j)

questions.explanation: In a diagonal matrix only the main-diagonal entries a11, a22, a33, ... may be non-zero, for example [[3, 0, 0],[0, 7, 0],[0, 0, 1]]. Option B reverses the idea by making the diagonal zero, and option C is the definition of a skew-symmetric matrix.

questions.question: Which of the following defines a scalar matrix?

options.a: A square matrix whose main-diagonal elements are all zero
options.b: A matrix in which every element is equal to the same number k
options.c: Any matrix that has been multiplied by a scalar k
options.d: A diagonal matrix whose diagonal elements are all equal

questions.explanation: A scalar matrix is a diagonal matrix with the same number k in every diagonal position, such as [[3, 0, 0],[0, 3, 0],[0, 0, 3]] = 3I. Option B wrongly puts k in the off-diagonal positions too, and option C describes scalar multiplication kA, which can produce any kind of matrix.

questions.question: Which of the following defines a rectangular matrix?

options.a: A matrix in which the number of rows equals the number of columns
options.b: A matrix in which every element is zero
options.c: A matrix in which the number of rows is not equal to the number of columns (m != n)
options.d: A square matrix with 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere

questions.explanation: A rectangular matrix has m rows and n columns with m != n, for example [[1, 2, 3],[4, 5, 6]], which is 2 x 3. Option A is the definition of a square matrix, option B describes the null matrix, and option D describes the identity matrix.

questions.question: Evaluate the determinant of A = [[2, 3, -1],[1, 1, 0],[2, -3, 5]]. What does the result show?
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row, |A| = 2(1 x 5 - 0 x (-3)) - 3(1 x 5 - 0 x 2) + (-1)(1 x (-3) - 1 x 2) = 10 - 15 + 5 = 0. A square matrix with zero determinant is singular, so it has no inverse. Option A comes from adding the middle term instead of subtracting it, option C slips on the sign of the last term, and option D gets the value right but the conclusion wrong, since non-singular means |A| != 0.

questions.question: Which statement about A = [[1, 2, 3],[2, 4, -3],[3, -3, 6]] is true?

options.c: A is symmetric, because A^t = A

questions.explanation: Interchanging the rows and columns of A gives the same matrix, since a12 = a21 = 2, a13 = a31 = 3 and a23 = a32 = -3, so A^t = A and A is symmetric. Option A is wrong because a skew-symmetric matrix needs zeros on the main diagonal and opposite-sign pairs, and option B is wrong because |A| = 1(24 - 9) - 2(12 + 9) + 3(-6 - 12) = 15 - 42 - 54 = -81, not 0.

questions.question: Evaluate the determinant of [[b, -1, a],[a, b, 0],[1, a, b]].
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row: b(b x b - 0 x a) - (-1)(a x b - 0 x 1) + a(a x a - b x 1) = b^3 + ab + a^3 - ab = a^3 + b^3. The two ab terms cancel only when the middle term is handled correctly; option B forgets that subtracting -1 times the minor adds ab. Option C comes from writing the last minor as a^2 + b instead of a^2 - b.

questions.question: Evaluate the determinant of [[1, 2, -2],[-1, 1, -3],[2, 4, -1]].
questions.explanation: Expanding along the first row: 1(1 x (-1) - (-3)(4)) - 2((-1)(-1) - (-3)(2)) + (-2)((-1)(4) - (1)(2)) = 1(11) - 2(7) - 2(-6) = 11 - 14 + 12 = 9. Option C adds the middle term instead of subtracting it (11 + 14 + 12), and option A slips on the first minor by taking -1 - 12 = -13.

questions.question: Find x and y if [[2, 1],[-3, 2]] = [[x + 3, 1],[-3, 3y - 4]].
questions.explanation: Equal matrices have equal corresponding elements, so x + 3 = 2 and 3y - 4 = 2. Hence x = 2 - 3 = -1, and 3y = 6 gives y = 2. Option C adds 3 instead of subtracting it, and option A stops at 3y = 6 without dividing by 3.

questions.question: Find x and y if [[x + 3, 1],[-3, 3y - 4]] = [[y, 1],[-3, 2x]].
questions.explanation: Matching corresponding elements gives x + 3 = y and 3y - 4 = 2x. Substituting y = x + 3 gives 3(x + 3) - 4 = 2x, so 3x + 5 = 2x and x = -5, then y = -5 + 3 = -2. Option D forgets to multiply the 3 inside the bracket (3x + 3 - 4 = 2x), and option C swaps the values of x and y.

questions.question: If A = [[1, -1, 2],[3, 2, 5],[-1, 0, 4]] and B = [[2, 1, -1],[1, 3, 4],[-1, 2, 1]], find A - B.
questions.explanation: Subtract element by element: for example 1 - 2 = -1, 2 - (-1) = 3 and -1 - (-1) = 0, giving A - B = [[-1, -2, 3],[2, -1, 1],[0, -2, 3]]. Option A is B - A (every sign reversed), option D is A + B, and option C wrongly treats 2 - (-1) as 1.

questions.question: Find the inverse of A = [[2, 1],[6, 3]].

options.b: The inverse does not exist, because |A| = 0

questions.explanation: |A| = 2(3) - 1(6) = 6 - 6 = 0, so A is singular and A^-1 = adj A/|A| would mean dividing by zero; the inverse does not exist (row 2 is just 3 times row 1). Option A wrongly takes the determinant as 6 + 6 = 12, and option D is only the adjoint, which is not an inverse.

questions.question: Find k if A = [[4, k, 3],[7, 3, 6],[2, 3, 1]] is a singular matrix.
questions.explanation: Set |A| = 0: 4(3 x 1 - 6 x 3) - k(7 x 1 - 6 x 2) + 3(7 x 3 - 3 x 2) = 4(-15) - k(-5) + 3(15) = -60 + 5k + 45 = 5k - 15. So 5k - 15 = 0 and k = 3. Option A comes from adding the middle term instead of subtracting it (-15 - 5k = 0), and option C stops at 5k = 15 without dividing by 5.

questions.question: Which of the following defines the minor of an element of a matrix?

options.a: The product of the element and its cofactor
options.b: The determinant left after deleting the row and the column in which the element lies
options.c: The determinant left after deleting only the row in which the element lies
options.d: The determinant left after deleting the row and column of the element, multiplied by (-1)^(i+j)

questions.explanation: The minor M_ij of the element a_ij is the determinant that remains when row i and column j are crossed out; for example, in [[3, 1, -4],[2, 5, 6],[1, 4, 8]] the minor of 3 is |5 6; 4 8| = 40 - 24 = 16. Option D is the cofactor, which attaches the sign (-1)^(i+j) to the minor, and option C does not leave a square array, so it cannot give a determinant.

questions.question: Which of the following defines the cofactor of an element of a matrix?

options.a: The element multiplied by its minor
options.b: The minor of the element with no change of sign
options.c: The minor of the element multiplied by (-1)^(i+j), that is C_ij = (-1)^(i+j) M_ij

questions.explanation: The cofactor attaches a place sign to the minor: C_ij = (-1)^(i+j) M_ij, so it equals the minor when i + j is even and its negative when i + j is odd. For example, in [[3, 1, -4],[2, 5, 6],[1, 4, 8]] the element 4 in row 3, column 2 has minor 26 and cofactor (-1)^5 x 26 = -26. Option B is just the minor, and option D puts the sign on the element itself instead of on its minor.

questions.question: Without expanding, the value of the determinant of [[alpha, beta + gamma, 1],[beta, gamma + alpha, 1],[gamma, alpha + beta, 1]] is
questions.explanation: Adding column 1 to column 2 does not change the determinant and makes every entry of column 2 equal to alpha + beta + gamma. Taking out this common factor leaves a column of 1s identical to column 3, and a determinant with two identical columns is 0. Option D is only the factor taken out, and it multiplies a determinant that is already zero.

questions.question: What are the minor and the cofactor of the element 3 (row 1, column 1) in the matrix [[3, 1, -4],[2, 5, 6],[1, 4, 8]]?
questions.explanation: Deleting row 1 and column 1 leaves [[5, 6],[4, 8]], so M11 = 5(8) - 6(4) = 40 - 24 = 16. The cofactor is C11 = (-1)^(1+1) x 16 = +16, since 1 + 1 is even. Option D gives the wrong sign, and option A adds the cross products (40 + 24) instead of subtracting them.

questions.question: What are the minor and the cofactor of the element 4 (row 3, column 2) in the matrix [[3, 1, -4],[2, 5, 6],[1, 4, 8]]?
questions.explanation: Deleting row 3 and column 2 leaves [[3, -4],[2, 6]], so M32 = 3(6) - (-4)(2) = 18 + 8 = 26. The cofactor is C32 = (-1)^(3+2) x 26 = -26, because 3 + 2 is odd. Option D forgets the sign, and option C treats -(-4)(2) as -8, giving 18 - 8 = 10.

questions.question: If A = [[1, 2],[3, 4]] and B = [[2, 3],[4, 5]], find A + B.
questions.explanation: Matrices of the same order are added element by element: A + B = [[1 + 2, 2 + 3],[3 + 4, 4 + 5]] = [[3, 5],[7, 9]]. Option B is A - B, option C multiplies corresponding elements, and option A is the matrix product AB.

questions.question: If A = [[1, 2],[3, 4]] and B = [[2, 3],[4, 5]], find A - B.
questions.explanation: Subtract corresponding elements: A - B = [[1 - 2, 2 - 3],[3 - 4, 4 - 5]] = [[-1, -1],[-1, -1]]. Option A is B - A, which reverses every sign, and option C is A + B.

questions.question: If A = [[1, 2],[3, 4]] and B = [[2, 3],[4, 5]], find AB.
questions.explanation: Each element of AB is a row of A times a column of B: AB = [[1(2) + 2(4), 1(3) + 2(5)],[3(2) + 4(4), 3(3) + 4(5)]] = [[10, 13],[22, 29]]. Option C is BA, which differs because matrix multiplication is not commutative, option B just multiplies corresponding elements, and option D multiplies rows of A by rows of B.

questions.question: If [[2, 3],[4, k]] is singular, find k.
questions.explanation: A singular matrix has zero determinant, so 2k - 3(4) = 0, giving 2k = 12 and k = 6. Option D adds the cross product instead of subtracting it (2k + 12 = 0), and option B multiplies the wrong pairs (2 x 4 - 3k = 0).

questions.question: Find A^-1 if A = [[5, 3],[1, 1]].
questions.explanation: |A| = 5(1) - 3(1) = 2, and the adjoint of a 2 x 2 matrix swaps the diagonal elements and changes the signs of the other two, giving adj A = [[1, -3],[-1, 5]]. So A^-1 = (1/2)[[1, -3],[-1, 5]] = [[1/2, -3/2],[-1/2, 5/2]]. Option B forgets the sign changes, option D forgets to swap 5 and 1, and option A uses 5 + 3 = 8 as the determinant.

questions.question: The order of the matrix [[2],[3],[4]] is
questions.explanation: The order of a matrix is written as rows x columns. [[2],[3],[4]] has 3 rows and 1 column, so it is a 3 x 1 column matrix. Option D (1 x 3) reverses the order and would describe a row matrix such as [2 3 4].

questions.question: The order of the matrix [1 2 3] is
questions.explanation: This matrix has 1 row and 3 columns, so its order (rows x columns) is 1 x 3, which makes it a row matrix. Option B (3 x 1) puts columns before rows and would describe a column matrix.

questions.question: Two matrices A and B are conformable for multiplication (AB can be formed) if:

options.a: Number of columns in A = number of rows in B
options.b: Number of columns in A = number of columns in B
options.c: Number of rows in A = number of rows in B

questions.explanation: AB can only be formed when each row of A has as many entries as each column of B, that is, the number of columns in A equals the number of rows in B. For example, a 2 x 3 matrix can multiply a 3 x 4 matrix to give a 2 x 4 product. Options B and C compare columns with columns or rows with rows, which does not let the rows of A be paired with the columns of B.

questions.question: If the order of matrix A is p x q and the order of matrix B is q x r, then the order of AB is:
questions.explanation: When A is p x q and B is q x r, the inner numbers (q and q) match, and the product takes the outer numbers, so AB is p x r. Option A is simply the order of A, while options B and D reverse or mix up the dimensions.

questions.question: In an identity matrix, all the diagonal elements are:
questions.explanation: An identity matrix is a square matrix with 1 in every position on the leading diagonal and 0 everywhere else, which is why AI = IA = A. Option A describes the off-diagonal elements, not the diagonal ones, and a diagonal of 2s (option B) would double a matrix instead of leaving it unchanged.

questions.question: The value of the determinant of [[2, 0],[1, 3]] is:
questions.explanation: For a 2 x 2 matrix [[a, b],[c, d]] the determinant is ad - bc, so here it is (2)(3) - (0)(1) = 6 - 0 = 6. Option B comes from a sign slip, and option D wrongly assumes that one zero element makes the whole determinant zero.

questions.question: If two rows of a determinant are identical, then its value is:
questions.explanation: Subtracting one identical row from the other produces a row of zeros without changing the determinant, so its value must be 0; for example, the determinant of [[1, 2],[1, 2]] is (1)(2) - (2)(1) = 0. Options A and C confuse this with other rules: swapping two rows changes the sign, but identical rows always give zero.

questions.question: If A = [[2, 3, 4],[0, 1, -1],[2, 0, 1]], then the cofactor of the element 4 is:
questions.explanation: The element 4 is in row 1, column 3, so its minor is the determinant left after deleting row 1 and column 3: M13 = |[0, 1],[2, 0]| = (0)(0) - (1)(2) = -2. The cofactor is C13 = (-1)^(1+3) x M13 = (+1)(-2) = -2. Option B is what you get from a sign slip or from deleting the wrong column, so always check which row and column you remove.

questions.question: If all the elements of a row or a column are zero, then the value of the determinant is:
questions.explanation: Expanding a determinant along a row (or column) of zeros multiplies every cofactor by 0, so the whole determinant equals 0. Options A and B have no basis, because the value does not depend on the other elements at all once a full row or column is zero.

questions.question: For what value of m is the matrix [[2, 3],[6, m]] singular?
questions.explanation: A matrix is singular when its determinant is zero. Here |A| = (2)(m) - (3)(6) = 2m - 18, and 2m - 18 = 0 gives m = 9. Option A (m = 6) gives |A| = 12 - 18 = -6 and option C (m = 8) gives 16 - 18 = -2, so neither makes the determinant zero.

questions.question: If [a_ij] and [b_ij] are of the same order and a_ij = b_ij for every i and j, then the two matrices are:
questions.explanation: Two matrices are equal when they have the same order and every pair of corresponding elements is the same, which is exactly the condition given. Singular (option A) refers to a zero determinant and null (option B) to a matrix of all zeros, neither of which follows from a_ij = b_ij.

questions.question: A matrix [a_ij] of order m x n is a row matrix if:
questions.explanation: A row matrix has only one row, so in an m x n matrix the number of rows m must be 1; for example [2, 5, 7] has order 1 x 3. Option D (n = 1) describes a column matrix, while options A and B refer to the position indices i and j, not to the size of the matrix.

questions.question: A matrix [c_ij] of order m x n is a rectangular (non-square) matrix if:
questions.explanation: A rectangular matrix is one whose number of rows is not equal to its number of columns, so m - n != 0 (that is, m != n), as in a 2 x 3 matrix. Option C (m = n) is the condition for a square matrix, and options A and B describe the positions of elements (off the diagonal and on it), not the shape of the matrix.

questions.question: A square matrix A = [a_ij] is a scalar matrix if:

options.b: a_ij = k for all i = j
options.c: a_ij = k for all i != j
options.d: a_ij = 0 for all i != j and a_ij = k for all i = j

questions.explanation: A scalar matrix is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal elements are all equal, so it needs both conditions together: 0 off the diagonal (i != j) and the same constant k on the diagonal (i = j). Option A alone only describes a diagonal matrix, whose diagonal entries could differ, and option B alone says nothing about the off-diagonal entries. Option C puts k in the wrong positions.

questions.question: A square matrix A = [a_ij] is an identity matrix if:

options.d: a_ij = 1 for all i = j and a_ij = 0 for all i != j

questions.explanation: An identity matrix has 1 in every diagonal position and 0 everywhere else, so it needs both conditions: a_ij = 1 when i = j and a_ij = 0 when i != j. Option A puts zeros on the diagonal, which is wrong, and options B and C on their own each give only half of the definition.

questions.question: If A = [a_ij] is of order m x n, then the order of kA (k a scalar) is:
questions.explanation: Multiplying a matrix by a scalar k multiplies every element by k but does not add or remove any rows or columns, so kA has the same order as A, m x n. Options B, C and D wrongly treat k as if it changed the number of rows or columns.

questions.question: For square matrices A and B of the same order, (A - B)^2 = A^2 - 2AB + B^2 if and only if:
questions.explanation: Expanding carefully, (A - B)^2 = (A - B)(A - B) = A^2 - AB - BA + B^2, because matrix multiplication is not commutative. This equals A^2 - 2AB + B^2 only when AB + BA = 2AB, that is BA = AB, or AB - BA = 0. Options A, C and D are conditions that do not force AB and BA to be equal, so they do not guarantee the identity.

questions.question: If A and B are symmetric matrices of the same order, then AB is always equal to:
questions.explanation: A symmetric matrix equals its own transpose, so A^t = A and B^t = B, which makes A^t B^t = AB true for every pair of symmetric matrices. Options A and C are tempting, but BA = B^t A^t = (AB)^t equals AB only when A and B commute; for example A = [[1, 2],[2, 3]] and B = [[0, 1],[1, 0]] give AB = [[2, 1],[3, 2]] but BA = [[2, 3],[1, 2]]. So option D is not true in general either.

questions.question: Define vectors C, S and Q as follows: C = (13, 7, 20, 15, 11) is the cost vector (naira per kg), S is the sales vector obtained by a mark-up of 35% on C, and Q = (1005, 2500, 675, 980, 2010) is the quantity vector (kg). Using the vector method, find the total cost and the total revenue.

options.a: Total cost = N80,875; total revenue = N124,423.08
options.b: Total cost = N80,875; total revenue = N109,181.25
options.c: Total cost = N109,181.25; total revenue = N80,875
options.d: Total cost = N80,875; total revenue = N28,306.25

questions.explanation: Total cost is the dot product C.Q = 13(1005) + 7(2500) + 20(675) + 15(980) + 11(2010) = N80,875. With S = 1.35C = (17.55, 9.45, 27, 20.25, 14.85), total revenue is S.Q = N109,181.25, which is 1.35 x 80,875 and leaves a profit of N28,306.25. Option D reports the profit (the 35% mark-up alone) as revenue, and option A treats 35% as a margin on the selling price rather than a mark-up on cost.

questions.question: A firm has 2 branches, A and B, each with 3 offices. In each office there are 3 peons, 4 clerks and 5 typists. In one office of branch A, 6 salesmen also work, and in each office of branch B, 2 head-clerks also work. Using row matrices in the order (peons, clerks, typists, salesmen, head-clerks), find the total number of posts of each kind in both branches taken together.
questions.explanation: Branch A gives [3,4,5,6,0] + [3,4,5,0,0] + [3,4,5,0,0] = [9,12,15,6,0], and branch B gives 3 x [3,4,5,0,2] = [9,12,15,0,6]. Adding the two branches gives [18,24,30,6,6]. Option B puts 6 salesmen in every office of branch A when only one office has them, and option C forgets that each of B's three offices has 2 head-clerks.

questions.question: A manufacturer produces 3 types of television sets, A, B and C. The sales matrix for 2 cities (rows City 1, City 2; columns A, B, C) is [[400,300,200],[300,200,100]]. The cost price of each set A, B, C is N1,000, N2,000 and N3,000 respectively, and the selling price is N1,500, N3,000 and N4,000 respectively. Using matrix algebra, find the total profit.
questions.explanation: Revenue is the sales matrix times the selling-price column: [[400,300,200],[300,200,100]] x [[1500],[3000],[4000]] = [[2300000],[1450000]], a total of N3,750,000. Cost is the same matrix times [[1000],[2000],[3000]] = [[1600000],[1000000]], a total of N2,600,000, so profit = 3,750,000 - 2,600,000 = N1,150,000. Option D is total revenue, option A is total cost, and option C is the profit from City 1 alone.

questions.question: A company with several retail stores sells the same line of products. The stock matrix S (rows = stores 1 to 4; columns = PCs, printers, monitors, modems) is [[120,145,130,85],[165,105,105,90],[110,115,95,80],[185,190,165,100]]. A PC costs N900, a printer N500, a monitor N350 and a modem N200. Expressing the prices as a column vector P, find the value V = SP of the stock in the four stores (in naira).
questions.explanation: Each store's stock value is its row of S multiplied by the price column P. For store 1, 120(900) + 145(500) + 130(350) + 85(200) = 108,000 + 72,500 + 45,500 + 17,000 = N243,000, and the same working gives N255,750, N205,750 and N339,250 for stores 2, 3 and 4. Option B matches the prices to the products in reverse order, option D leaves the modems out of the sum, and option A swaps the printer and monitor prices.

questions.question: Solve by Cramer's rule: 8x1 + 3x2 = 14 and 9x1 + 2x2 = 24.
questions.explanation: |A| = 8(2) - 3(9) = 16 - 27 = -11; replacing column 1 by the constants gives |A1| = 14(2) - 3(24) = -44, and replacing column 2 gives |A2| = 8(24) - 14(9) = 66. So x1 = -44/-11 = 4 and x2 = 66/-11 = -6, which checks: 8(4) + 3(-6) = 14 and 9(4) + 2(-6) = 24. Option C comes from taking |A| as +11, and option D drops the negative sign of |A| when finding x2.

questions.question: Given the demand and supply functions for two related markets: Qd(A) = 82 - 3PA + PB; Qd(B) = 92 + 2PA - 4PB; Qs(A) = -5 + 15PA; Qs(B) = -6 + 32PB, where Qd and Qs are quantity demanded and quantity supplied. Find the equilibrium price in each market (to 2 decimal places where necessary).
questions.explanation: Equilibrium in each market needs Qd = Qs: 82 - 3PA + PB = -5 + 15PA gives 18PA - PB = 87, and 92 + 2PA - 4PB = -6 + 32PB gives -2PA + 36PB = 98. With |A| = 18(36) - (-1)(-2) = 646, Cramer's rule gives PA = 3230/646 = 5 and PB = 1938/646 = 3. Option D swaps the two prices, option C ignores the cross-price terms and solves 18PA = 87 and 36PB = 98 separately, and option B gives the equilibrium quantities, not prices.

questions.question: Given the demand and supply functions for two related markets: Qd(A) = 82 - 3PA + PB; Qd(B) = 92 + 2PA - 4PB; Qs(A) = -5 + 15PA; Qs(B) = -6 + 32PB, where Qd and Qs are quantity demanded and quantity supplied. Find the equilibrium quantity in each market.
questions.explanation: Setting Qd = Qs in each market gives 18PA - PB = 87 and -2PA + 36PB = 98, whose solution is PA = 5 and PB = 3. Then QA = -5 + 15(5) = 70 and QB = -6 + 32(3) = 90, and the demand side agrees: 82 - 15 + 3 = 70 and 92 + 10 - 12 = 90. Option B adds the supply intercepts instead of subtracting them, and option A leaves the intercepts out completely.

questions.question: Solve the equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix: 5x - y + z = 4; 3x + 2y - 5z = 2; x + 3y - 2z = 5.
questions.explanation: |A| = 5(-4 + 15) + 1(-6 + 5) + 1(9 - 2) = 55 - 1 + 7 = 61, and adj(A) = [[11,1,3],[1,-11,28],[7,-16,13]]. Then X = (1/61) adj(A) B = (1/61)(44 + 2 + 15, 4 - 22 + 140, 28 - 32 + 65) = (1/61)(61, 122, 61) = (1, 2, 1), which satisfies all three equations, e.g. 5(1) - 2 + 1 = 4. Option C forgets to divide by the determinant, and options A and B fail the first equation.

questions.question: There are 3 types of food: I, II and III. Food I contains 1 unit each of nutrients A, B and C. Food II contains 1 unit of A, 2 units of B and 3 units of C. Food III contains 1, 3 and 4 units of A, B and C respectively. If 7 units of A, 16 units of B and 22 units of C are required, how many units of foods I, II and III respectively will provide exactly these amounts?
questions.explanation: The requirements give x + y + z = 7, x + 2y + 3z = 16 and x + 3y + 4z = 22. Subtracting the first equation from the other two gives y + 2z = 9 and 2y + 3z = 15, so z = 3, y = 3 and x = 7 - 3 - 3 = 1. The other three options also add up to 7 units of nutrient A, but they fail the nutrient B and C requirements; for example, option B (3, 3 and 1) gives only 3 + 6 + 3 = 12 units of nutrient B instead of 16.
